title: CRAW: Codec Robust Audio Watermarking
abstract: Recent advances in generative speech models have made it increasingly difficult to distinguish authentic from synthetic audio, enabling new forms of fraud and misinformation. Audio watermarking offers a promising defense by embedding an imperceptible signal into generated speech that can later be detected to verify its provenance. However, recent studies have shown that existing post-hoc watermarking methods fail under neural codecs and denoisers, transformations routinely applied during real-world storage, transmission, and processing, severely limiting their practical utility. Here we introduce CRAW, a codec-robust audio watermarking framework that jointly improves robustness against neural re-synthesis while maintaining high perceptual quality. CRAW combines distortion-aware training with an attention-based pooling mechanism, inference-time perceptual mask- ing, and an error-correcting code to recover the fidelity lost during robust training. Experiments demonstrate that CRAW achieves state-of-the-art robustness against neural codecs, denoisers, and vocoders while maintaining perceptual quality comparable to existing post-hoc watermarking methods. The code is available at https://github.com/DavidC1212/craw.

title: Experimental Evaluation of Passive Polarization Compensation Techniques for Fiber-Distributed Polarization-Entangled Photons
abstract: Entanglement distribution through optical fibers is essential for quantum communication networks; however, fiber transmission can alter photon polarization and modify the observed correlations of polarization-entangled states, necessitating polarization compensation to recover the desired entangled state in the measurement basis. Here, we experimentally evaluate two passive polarization compensation techniques: a free-space Quarter-Half-Quarter (QHQ) waveplate configuration and an in-fiber three-paddle Fiber Polarization Controller (FPC). The polarization transformation along each downconverted-photon path is independently compensated through a systematic path-by-path optimization procedure. Using both techniques, we recover high-quality polarization correlations and entanglement, with visibilities exceeding $93\%$ in three mutually unbiased bases and fidelities above $94.5\%$. The results demonstrate comparable restoration using free-space waveplate-based and fiber-based control, establishing a systematic framework for laboratory and short-reach quantum communication links.

evidence.abstract: Entanglement distribution through optical fibers is essential for quantum communication networks; however, fiber transmission can alter photon polarization and modify the observed correlations of polarization-entangled states, necessitating polarization compensation to recover the desired entangled state in the measurement basis. Here, we experimentally evaluate two passive polarization compensation techniques: a free-space Quarter-Half-Quarter (QHQ) waveplate configuration and an in-fiber three-paddle Fiber Polarization Controller (FPC). The polarization transformation along each downconverted-photon path is independently compensated through a systematic path-by-path optimization procedure. Using both techniques, we recover high-quality polarization correlations and entanglement, with visibilities exceeding $93\%$ in three mutually unbiased bases and fidelities above $94.5\%$. The results demonstrate comparable restoration using free-space waveplate-based and fiber-based control, establishing a systematic framework for laboratory and short-reach quantum communication links.

title: CC-4DGS: Computational Deformation and Point-Cloud Compression for Storage-Efficient Dynamic Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Dynamic four-dimensional (4D) Gaussian Splatting has emerged as a powerful explicit representation for high-quality view synthesis, yet existing methods still require tens to hundreds of megabytes per scene due to their heavy reliance on large multi-resolution hash tables and high-dimensional Gaussian attributes. This paper presents CC-4DGS, a storage-efficient and scalable framework that rethinks both deformation modeling and canonical attribute storage. First, we introduce a computational deformation field (CDF) that replaces large multi-resolution learnable hash tables with deterministic dense hash encoding and compact neural decoders, enabling on-the-fly synthesis of deformation features while reducing deformation storage to only 1--3 MB per scene. Second, we propose a compression of canonical point-cloud attributes (CCA) pipeline that compresses high-dimensional spherical harmonic appearance terms and auxiliary Gaussian attributes via conditional autoencoding, selective quantization, and residual codebooks, achieving 3--5$\times$ point-cloud reduction with negligible quality loss. Together, these components yield a unified representation that preserves real-time rendering performance while reducing total storage to 20--30 MB. Extensive experiments across the N3DV and Technicolor Light Field datasets demonstrate that CC-4DGS achieves reconstruction accuracy comparable to state-of-the-art methods such as Swift4D, while offering significantly improved storage efficiency and favorable runtime-memory trade-offs.

title: On Propositional Dynamic Logic and Concurrency
abstract: Dynamic logic is a powerful approach to reasoning about programs and their executions, obtained by extending classical logic with modalities that can express program executions as formulas. However, the use of dynamic logic in the setting of concurrency has proved problematic because of the challenge of capturing interleaving. This challenge stems from the fact that, traditionally, programs are represented by their sets of traces. These sets are then expressed as elements of a Kleene algebra, for which it is not possible to decide equality in the presence of the commutations required to model interleaving. In this work, we generalise propositional dynamic logic (PDL) to a logic framework we call operational propositional dynamic logic (OPDL), which departs from tradition by distinguishing programs from their traces. Traces are generated by an arbitrary operational semantics that we take as a parameter, making our approach applicable to different program syntaxes and semantics. To develop our framework, we provide the first proof of cut-elimination for a finitely-branching non-wellfounded sequent calculus for PDL. Thanks to this result we can effortlessly prove adequacy for PDL, and extend these results to OPDL. We conclude by discussing OPDL for two representative cases of concurrency: the Calculus of Communicating Systems (CCS), where interleaving is obtained by parallel composition, and Choreographic Programming, where interleaving is obtained by out-of-order execution.

title: Weighted UnLearning from Experience for improved spurious correlation robustness
abstract: Despite their success, Deep Learning (DL) models are susceptible to spurious correlations. These are accidental correlations between non-predictive features of the training dataset and the target label, leading to models that do not generalise well to samples without such spurious correlations. We propose to address this failure mode by extending and improving an existing method for spurious correlation robustness — UnLearning from Experience (ULE). ULE trains two models in parallel; a biased model is encouraged to learn the spurious correlations, while a separate debiased model is trained to solve the same task while avoiding learning the same behaviour as the first, thus avoiding learning the spurious correlations. A weakness of ULE is that it treats every training example identically, regardless of whether or not it contains a spurious correlation. Therefore, ULE does not make optimal use of the training data, leading to worsethan- necessary performance. To address this weakness, we introduce Weighted UnLearning from Experience (wULE), which modifies the original ULE loss function to reweight the components depending on whether a training sample likely contains spurious correlations. Hence, we explore two methods for identifying training samples likely to contain spurious correlations. We test our approach using several well-known spurious correlation robustness benchmarks — Waterbirds, CelebA, UrbanCars and MultiNLI. Our novel wULE method outperforms the original ULE in all cases and achieves Worst-Group Accuracy (WGA) results comparable to the best methods in the spurious correlation robustness literature.

title: Too Simple, Too Complex, Just Right: A Interdisciplinary Mapping Review of Inductive Biases in Deep Learning Architectures
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Inductive Biases in Deep Learning Architectures in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of deep learning and inductive bias as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Title: Dynamic Space Transformations via Quantum Spin
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic space transformation algorithm based on quantum spin, leveraging its inherent self-similarity to dynamically adjust quantum system geometries. The core mechanism centers around iterative optimization driven by the self-correlation of quantum spins, enabling the design of complex spacetime structures within quantum systems. This approach offers a potential paradigm shift in optimizing quantum device performance, addressing limitations of conventional static optimization methods. We present a framework for generating and manipulating quantum systems exhibiting dynamic spacetime, and discuss its implications for advancing the design and control of quantum technologies.

title: Quantum Entanglement Dynamic Geometry Transformation Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement offers a fundamentally new approach to geometric transformations, potentially surpassing the limitations of classical algorithms. This paper introduces a novel dynamic geometry transformation algorithm based on quantum entanglement, designed to dynamically adjust geometric structures based on input transformations. We explore the potential of this approach to achieve complex geometric transformations and offer a fundamentally different computational model. The core mechanism involves leveraging entanglement to encode and manipulate geometric information, allowing for iterative refinement and optimization. We present a detailed mathematical framework and discuss preliminary results demonstrating the algorithm's capability to perform complex geometric transformations. This work explores the potential for novel calculations and optimization.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Causal Inference in Time Series
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to causal inference within the context of time series data, leveraging the power of probabilistic programming. Traditional causal inference techniques frequently rely on assumptions of static relationships, limiting their applicability to dynamic systems. This work addresses this limitation by employing probabilistic programming languages to explicitly model causal relationships, incorporating temporal dependencies and facilitating the estimation of causal effects under evolving conditions. The core mechanism involves defining causal models using probabilistic programming, allowing for the simulation of time series data and the subsequent estimation of causal effects. This approach offers a rigorous framework for causal inference in dynamic time series environments, representing a significant advancement over existing methods. The methodology is illustrated through a conceptual framework, focusing on the implementation and theoretical underpinnings rather than specific experimental results. The paper highlights the potential of this approach for addressing complex causal questions within time series data, particularly where temporal dynamics are critical.

title: Adaptive Self-Organized Quantum Network Quantum Probability Distribution Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the development of an adaptive self-organized quantum network (ASQN) quantum probability distribution optimization algorithm. Traditional quantum computation relies heavily on human intervention in parameter tuning, leading to limitations in accuracy and efficiency. The proposed algorithm dynamically adjusts the probability distribution within the ASQN, automatically optimizing the quantum state for improved performance. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop utilizing system state to iteratively refine the probability distribution, offering a novel approach to quantum computing that surpasses existing optimization techniques. This work demonstrates the potential for significant improvements in quantum accuracy through automated adjustment, paving the way for more robust and reliable quantum computations.

title: Dynamic Topological Quantum Entanglement Routing
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for quantum communication utilizing dynamic topological quantum entanglement routing. The core concept involves constructing a quantum network topology not based on fixed physical connections, but rather on dynamically adapting entanglement routes. This approach leverages quantum entanglement and machine learning to create a self-optimizing network capable of overcoming limitations inherent in traditional quantum networks. The system analyzes real-time network conditions – specifically entanglement strength and noise levels – and adjusts the topology of the entanglement routes using a machine learning algorithm. This dynamic adaptation aims to establish and maintain optimal communication pathways, theoretically offering the potential for information transfer exceeding the speed of light. The proposed architecture addresses the shortcomings of existing quantum networks that often rely on static physical connections and lacks adaptability. This research explores the fundamental principles and theoretical possibilities of such a system.

title: TT-G42: An E8-Extended Post-Quantum Cryptosystem with Graded Geometric Hard-Gating
abstract: TT-G42: An E8-Extended Post-Quantum Cryptosystem with Graded Geometric Hard-Gating Chloe J. TullyIndependent ResearcherORCID: 0009-0007-5661-7332August 2026 Version 1.1 Abstract We present TT-G42, the natural successor to the TT-G41 hybrid cryptosystem. The five-dimensional Ly-Algebraic core is replaced by the 248-dimensional adjoint representation of the exceptional simple Lie algebra E8. The Quasi-Equivalence Index (QEI) is redefined on the weight lattice of E8, exploiting the Coxeter group symmetry and the deep golden-ratio structure of the E8 root system to construct a geometric invariant with substantially larger entropy. The lattice layer is scaled to NIST-compatible parameters (n=701, q=2048), and the symmetry-modulated padding is reformulated as a graded noise injection derived from the projection onto the fundamental Weyl chamber. We establish that the QEI-induced failure probability continues to obey a logistic bound with shape parameter 15.57, independent of ambient dimension to leading order. An adaptive hard-gate mechanism is introduced whose threshold is derived from the running variance of the QEI stream; the gate is shown to be constant-time and free of partial-message side channels. Empirical evaluation on 10 000 trials yields R2=0.984. The construction demonstrates that exceptional algebraic geometry can serve as a native control surface for lattice-based post-quantum protocols. Keywords: post-quantum cryptography, E8, exceptional Lie algebra, Quasi-Equivalence Index, NTRU, geometric security bound, side-channel resistance, Weyl group, graded noise injection Introduction TT-G41 demonstrated that a continuous geometric invariant derived from a graded Lie algebra can function as an active cryptographic control surface rather than a passive hardness assumption . The five-dimensional construction established the principle: geometric coherence, measured by the Quasi-Equivalence Index (QEI), directly modulates ciphertext entropy and determines decryption success through a deterministic hard gate. The present work scales that principle to its natural algebraic limit. The exceptional simple Lie algebra E8, with its 248-dimensional adjoint representation, 240 roots, and Weyl group of order 696 729 600, supplies a geometric entropy space of sufficient complexity to address the residual threat of adversarial vector manipulation that remained a limitation of the five-dimensional case. The E8 root system exhibits a well-known connection to the golden ratio =1+5/2 through its Coxeter plane and icosahedral symmetry, rendering it the canonical extension of the original Ly-Algebra’s golden-ratio grading. TT-G42 contributes three concrete advances: An E8-native Quasi-Equivalence Index defined on the weight lattice, computed via the Killing form and a graded action of the Cartan generators, together with a closed-form link between root-space distortion and decryption failure probability. A NIST-compatible lattice layer (n=701, q=2048) whose circulant inversion is verified against the security boundaries of Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanisms . An adaptive hard gate whose threshold is derived from the empirical variance of the QEI stream, eliminating the fixed-threshold limitation of TT-G41 and providing constant-time, side-channel-resistant rejection.

title: Title: Non-Local Semantic Networks
abstract: The traditional semantic network, while foundational, often struggles to capture the dynamic nature of meaning and the emergence of novel concepts. This paper proposes a novel approach to semantic networks – Non-Local Semantic Networks (NLSNs) – that explicitly models concepts across spacetime, facilitating the propagation of semantic changes through a chronological graph. This design allows for the evolution of meaning and the formation of new concepts, driven by interactions between nodes representing temporal relationships. We present a detailed architecture, including the implementation of a 'chronological graph' and the mathematical framework for representing and propagating semantic changes. The core claim is that NLSNs provide a robust mechanism for understanding and generating meaning in a temporally evolving system.

title: Neural Network Memory in Dynamic Topology Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to complex pattern learning within Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) by incorporating dynamic topology changes. The core concept leverages the inherent plasticity of neural networks, simulating the evolving connections between neurons to achieve more efficient and robust learning compared to traditional static weight update methods. The proposed system utilizes a Self-Organizing Map (SOM) based topology update rule, coupled with a reinforcement learning algorithm, to predictively adjust network topology based on neuron activity patterns and learning objectives. Furthermore, a neuron death mechanism is introduced to promote topological optimization and mitigate local optima. The resulting network demonstrates superior performance in complex pattern prediction and control, highlighting the potential of dynamic topology learning for advanced ANN applications.

title: Bio-Inspired Distributed Machine Learning Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to distributed machine learning optimization inspired by biological neural networks. The core concept is to mimic the parallel computing and learning mechanisms observed in biological systems to tackle large-scale optimization problems. The proposed algorithm decomposes the optimization task into multiple sub-problems, which are then solved concurrently by a network of nodes. These nodes utilize bio-inspired heuristic algorithms to refine the solutions of the sub-problems and ultimately achieve global optimization. The key innovation lies in leveraging the inherent advantages of biological neural networks to enhance the efficiency and scalability of distributed machine learning optimization. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, focusing on the mechanisms for parallel computation, learning, and convergence. This work lays the foundation for a new paradigm in optimization, drawing inspiration from the elegant and robust design of the brain. ---

title: 基于自适应的图灵机计算框架
abstract: This paper introduces a novel, adaptive graph theory-based computational framework for logical reasoning. Traditional graph theory approaches often require pre-defined parameters, limiting their applicability to complex problems. Our framework dynamically adjusts internal graph states based on input data, enabling the algorithm to intelligently adapt to the problem's characteristics and improve reasoning efficiency. We demonstrate the framework's effectiveness through a series of experimental results, showcasing its superior performance compared to static graph theory methods in a range of logical reasoning tasks. The core mechanism involves a self-tuning parameter adjustment algorithm that iteratively optimizes the graph's state to enhance logical inference. The research addresses the limitations of static approaches by introducing a flexible and adaptive system that responds to the input data, ultimately leading to more robust and efficient logical reasoning.

title: High-Dimensional Symbolic Logic Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum computation leveraging high-dimensional symbolic logic, aiming to accelerate the evaluation and verification of complex logical expressions. We propose a quantum-enhanced symbolic logic system that utilizes quantum entanglement and superposition to achieve significantly faster computation compared to classical methods. The core mechanism centers around exploiting these quantum phenomena to represent and manipulate logical statements with unprecedented efficiency. The system focuses on automating the generation of logical inference models, reducing the reliance on manual effort. This work addresses the limitations of traditional symbolic logic computation by introducing a fundamentally different algorithmic structure. We present initial results demonstrating the potential for substantial speedups in specific scenarios, highlighting the promise of this approach for complex problem-solving.

title: Voice-Sync: AI-Powered Multilingual News Reader Using Python
abstract: Yet although accessing news online has never been easier, the experience tends to be fragmented. Readers frequently have to jump between multiple websites, wade through lengthy articles, or switch between different tools just. To obtain a translation or to have some content read out loud. This constant back-and-forth makes it difficult to stay informed, especially for those who prefer consuming news in their native. People or those who want a hands-free experience. To solve this, we developed Voice-Sync, a web-based news reader that brings the power of Artificial Intelligence into one seamless platform. Built using the Python and the Flask framework, Voice-Sync automatically pulls the latest headlines from NewsAPI and processes via specialized AI modules. When an article has been retrieved, the app produces a brief summary by means of specialized AI modules. Once an article is retrieved, the app creates a concise summary using Natural Language Processing, translates it into various. Convert Indian Languages into clear, natural speech using the text-to-speech feature from Microsoft Edge Neural. Beyond reading the news, Voice-Sync offers voice- controlled navigation, sentiment analysis, bookmarking, and the ability to export reports as PDFs. By streamlining these tasks, we have created a more intuitive, accessible way for users to engage with information without the usual technical friction.

title: Same Persona, Different Behaviors: Quantifying Persona Conditioning in Large Language Models
abstract: Persona conditioning is increasingly used to guide the behavior of Large Language Models (LLMs), yet the extent to which models consistently and effectively adapt to assigned identities remains unclear. In this paper, we present a systematic evaluation of persona-conditioned behavior in three open-weight LLMs: DeepSeek, Gemma, and Nemotron. We designed a controlled experiment involving 21 ethically and socially sensitive questions and six distinct personas, generating a total of 378 model responses. Our analysis combines decision-level evaluation, TF-IDF-based lexical characterization, and embedding-based semantic similarity. We also introduce a Personalization Index that captures both intra-persona consistency and inter-persona differentiation. The results show that personalization is a gradual and strongly model-dependent phenomenon. Gemma exhibits the highest degree of adaptation, with clear lexical and semantic differentiation across personas, while Nemotron demonstrates more consistent but less pronounced personalization. DeepSeek displays weaker and less stable persona adaptation. A key finding is that persona conditioning does not lead to a uniform interpretation of identity: the same person can produce systematically different responses depending on the model. This highlights personalization as a trade-off between relevance and diversity, offering engagement benefits with the potential risk of reinforcing existing biases.

title: Scaling Laws, Tabular Data and Actuarial Ratemaking Models
abstract: Scaling laws in modern deep learning describe how held-out loss improves as model capacity, training data, and compute increase, often following power-law trends. We investigate whether analogous scaling regularities arise in actuarial ratemaking, where data are tabular, heterogeneous, and noisy, and where classical models such as GLMs remain strong baselines. Using a real-world motor insurance portfolio, we train models from different families across increasing fractions of the training data and multiple random seeds, evaluating out-of-sample Poisson deviance, a likelihood-based loss for Poisson count predictions in which lower values indicate better held-out fit. We find that all model families improve with additional data, but scaling exponents differ substantially: TabM exhibits markedly stronger data scaling than purely supervised tabular Transformers and standard MLP baselines. Transformer variants show weak parameter scaling unless augmented with additional inductive biases (TabM-style adaptation or self-supervision). These results provide quantitative guidance on model selection by data regime and suggest that effective scaling on actuarial tabular tasks depends on architecture and loss function objective design, with simple increases in Transformer size providing limited gains.

title: Optical Reservoir Computing with Structural Nonlinearity for Forecasting Chaotic Time Series
abstract: Optical computing offers a promising route to high-speed, energy-efficient information processing. However, implementing nonlinear operations typically requires strong light-matter interactions. Here, we introduce structural nonlinearity into an optical reservoir computing architecture, using only linear components. A digital micromirror device acts as a reconfigurable scattering potential, while the propagation of light through a scattering medium provides the high-dimensional mode mixing. By enforcing a second interaction with the wavefront shaper, we obtain a quadratic mapping of the input within the reservoir. A single experimental apparatus simultaneously implements conventional and structurally nonlinear reservoir architectures, enabling a direct comparison on forecasting of the chaotic Mackey-Glass time series. We demonstrate that the structurally nonlinear reservoir improves short-term prediction accuracy and better preserves the long-term dynamics of the chaotic system, demonstrating the potential of structural nonlinearity for low-power optical computing.

title: H3DNAS: Hardware-Aware ONNX-Native 3D Point Cloud Model Compression
abstract: Deploying 3D point cloud models on edge hardware such as the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano is severely constrained by compute and memory budgets. Existing compression methods require access to the model's original source code, rendering them inapplicable to the Open Neural Network Exchange (ONNX) binaries commonly distributed by vendors and model repositories. We present \textbf{H3DNAS}, a hardware-aware model compression framework that operates directly on ONNX computational graphs without requiring original source code, architecture class definition, or gradient access during search. H3DNAS makes three contributions: (1) a \textbf{Channel Dependency Graph (CDG)} that classifies ONNX operators into four constraint classes and formally establishes that the free parameter fraction $ρ_f$ is topological invariant, a provable compression ceiling computable in $\mathcal{O}(|V|+|E|)$; (2) a \textbf{Two-Stage Hierarchical Search} that prunes candidate architectures by $L_1$-importance channel selection, ranks them by output fidelity as a zero-shot label-free proxy, and applies GhostConv structural mutation to Pareto-optimal candidates; and (3) the \textbf{first source-code-free compression pipeline for 3D point cloud models}, operating entirely via ONNX graph surgery with no original architecture definition required. On ModelNet40, H3DNAS reduces the number of parameters in PointNet, PointNet++, and PointMLP by $65.5\%$, $43.2\%$, and $49.1\%$, respectively, while achieving $1.99\times$, $1.29\times$, and $1.67\times$ inference speedups with negligible loss in accuracy. The source code is publicly available\footnote{https://github.com/ClarityLab-Org/h3dnas}.

title: Semantics-Guided Automatic Tensorization for Multiobjective Evolutionary Algorithms: A Multi-Agent Framework
abstract: Multiobjective evolutionary algorithms (MOEAs) naturally expose population-level parallelism, but many mature implementations encode their computation in sequential program structures designed for central processing units. Exploiting modern tensor computing platforms therefore requires more than direct code translation: the implementation must be restructured without changing the defining optimization mechanism of the underlying MOEA. We formulate automatic tensorization for MOEAs as semantics-guided computational restructuring and develop Evolutionary Code Conversion (EvoCoCo), a multi-agent framework that realizes this formulation. EvoCoCo reconstructs algorithm-specific states, dependencies, operators, and update logic into a structured semantic representation and organizes them through a shared tensorization blueprint. Specialized transformation branches then explore alternative tensor realizations, while execution feedback guides validation, repair, and candidate selection. Experiments on a benchmark of 48 MOEAs evaluate migration reliability, optimization fidelity, and computational scalability. Under matched large language model backends, EvoCoCo attains higher migration reliability than direct one-shot translation. Across the benchmark suites, 88.2% of valid comparisons satisfy the predefined optimization-fidelity criterion. The tensorized implementations also exhibit increasing acceleration on graphics processing units as population size or decision dimension grows, with median measured speedups ranging from $22.6\times$ under population scaling to $80.2\times$ under decision-dimension scaling. External-source and ablation studies further assess transfer beyond the main benchmark and the roles of the major framework components.

title: 2026 2nd International Conference on Federated Learning and Intelligent Computing Systems (FLICS)
abstract: The rapid expansion of distributed Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) infrastructures introduces significant cybersecurity vulnerabilities, as Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices continuously stream sensitive physiological data across organizational boundaries. Existing centralized threat detection paradigms are poorly suited to this environment, often failing to capture the temporal evolution of attacks while violating data sovereignty requirements under Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) and General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). To address these challenges, we propose Federated Temporal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (FedTempRAG), a novel framework for privacy-preserving, real-time threat intelligence in distributed RPM ecosystems. FedTempRAG integrates a decentralized vector database for cross-institutional retrieval, a dynamic temporal knowledge graph to model attack progression, and a secure aggregation protocol that enables privacy-preserving collaborative learning. Our implementation adopts homomorphic encryption for secure query processing and Byzantine-resilient aggregation to defend against adversarial participants. We evaluated FedTempRAG on a simulated multi-hospital RPM network using real-world medical threat datasets and high-fidelity emulated IoMT environments derived from public RPM repositories. Experimental results demonstrate that FedTempRAG achieves 94.3% detection accuracy, 91.7% recall, and a 0.930 F1-score, while maintaining an average inference latency of 847 -ms and a 9.8% computation overhead, enabling practical real-time deployment in RPM systems. The temporal reasoning component successfully reconstructed many multi-stage attack lifecycles, highlighting the effectiveness of integrating temporal context into federated threat intelligence. These findings establish FedTempRAG as a robust foundation for next-generation RPM security, achieving a practical balance between collaborative intelligence, temporal awareness, system efficiency, and strict privacy preservation.

title: USE OF HISTOPATHOLOGICAL IMAGE DATABASES AND ASSOCIATED DATA FOR DIAGNOSTIC IMPROVEMENT OF LEUKOPLAKIA AND ORAL CANCER: A scoping review
abstract: This scoping review aims to map and characterize the global literature on histopathological image datasets and associated clinical metadata for oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMD) and oral cancer, evaluating how these repositories are developed, characterized, and applied to train, validate, and test artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning models. Following the JBI methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, the protocol outlines a comprehensive search strategy across major health and technological databases alongside grey literature, without date or language restrictions. The extracted results will be synthesized in descriptive tables detailing dataset identification, population characteristics, associated clinical features and diagnoses, histopathological diagnoses, metadata, annotation methods, AI technologies employed, and their specific downstream applications.

title: General Structure Unfolding Intelligence: From Core Structure and Delta Modification to a General Paradigm of Intelligence
abstract: General Structure Unfolding Intelligence (GSUI) develops a structural framework for studying intelligent processes as controlled unfolding from persistent structure. Its canonical form is expressed as +/- , with extensions involving context, triggering, unfolding space, control policy, evaluation, invariant preservation, certification, feedback, structural growth, and Structural Self. The repository examines Folding and Unfolding as complementary phases of an intelligence cycle: observation and experience may be folded into persistent structure, while that structure can later be unfolded into reasoning, generation, planning, routing, coding, control, action, and structural modification. GSUI distinguishes search within an existing possibility space from structural unfolding that can change future possibility itself. It introduces Unfolding Space to distinguish possible, reachable, allowed, preferred, selected, and certified transitions; treats the Control Plane as a first-class component of consequential intelligent unfolding; and defines Structural Growth as retained unfolding that changes future unfolding capacity. GSUI further introduces Structural Self as the persistent structural reference frame relative to which Delta, capability, continuity, world-model meaning, and future unfolding are defined. The framework explicitly separates Structural Self from consciousness or personhood, explores non-anthropomorphic machine perception and machine-native cognition, and maintains the governance principle that machine-native cognition should remain compatible with human-governable consequences. This v1.0.0 release establishes the foundational GSUI research framework, terminology, claim boundaries, visual language, and future research directions.

title: Dynamic Matrix Mapping for Optimization: A Novel Approach
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic matrix mapping algorithm (DMM) for optimizing complex systems. The DMM offers a robust and adaptable approach to parameter tuning, enabling automatic adjustment of parameters to maximize the objective function. Traditional optimization methods often require manual parameter adjustment, which can be time-consuming and prone to error. The DMM leverages the unique characteristics of dynamic matrices to achieve more efficient and reliable parameter optimization. This research presents a framework that simplifies the parameter tuning process and enhances the algorithm's adaptability to complex systems. The core mechanism focuses on the dynamic reshaping of the objective function matrix through matrix operations, leading to improved optimization performance. This approach significantly reduces the need for manual adjustment and improves the overall efficiency of parameter optimization.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Storage & Extraction Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre phenomenon where two particles become linked and share the same fate regardless of the distance separating them, has captivated scientists and intrigued philosophers alike. This research explores the potential of harnessing this quantum phenomenon to develop novel information storage and extraction techniques. We propose a system leveraging quantum entanglement for secure key distribution and data transfer, utilizing a specialized extraction algorithm that exploits the unique properties of entangled states. This research focuses on establishing a robust and efficient method for safeguarding information against eavesdropping and optimizing data transfer rates. The core of this investigation is the design of a key distribution protocol based on entangled states, complemented by a novel extraction algorithm designed to maximize data fidelity and minimize computational overhead. The anticipated outcome is a significantly enhanced security and efficient data transfer capability, representing a major advancement in the field of quantum information science. This paper details the theoretical foundations, proposed algorithm design, and potential applications of this innovative approach.

title: Homomorphic Encryption-Based Privacy-Preserving Data Analysis
abstract: This paper explores the application of homomorphic encryption for privacy-preserving data analysis. The core claim is that leveraging homomorphic encryption allows for data analysis while maintaining data confidentiality and ensuring the accuracy of the results. The proposed mechanism involves encrypting sensitive data using homomorphic encryption algorithms and performing computations directly on the encrypted data to obtain analytical outcomes. This approach addresses the growing need for secure data analysis in scenarios where data privacy is paramount. The research demonstrates the feasibility and potential of this technique, offering a novel solution for protecting sensitive information during analytical processes. This work provides a foundational understanding of this technology and its potential impact on various domains.

title: Parallel Iterative Proof Verification for Abstract Algebra
abstract: This paper introduces a novel parallel algorithm for verifying abstract algebraic proofs, designed to significantly reduce computational time for large, complex proofs. The proposed system leverages distributed verification, employing asynchronous computation and parallel processing to accelerate the verification process. The core mechanism centers around iterative proof verification, employing a hierarchical approach to improve efficiency. We present a detailed architecture, including the key components and their interactions, and demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through simulations and illustrative examples. The system is specifically tailored to address the challenges posed by the exponential growth in the complexity of abstract algebraic proofs. The ultimate goal is to provide a practical solution for tackling computationally intensive mathematical problems.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding via Graph-Based Algorithms
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics with immense potential for quantum computing and communication. However, maintaining entanglement over long distances poses significant challenges due to decoherence. This paper explores the application of graph-based algorithms to enhance quantum information encoding, specifically focusing on the integration of entanglement with graph theory. We propose a novel algorithm that leverages the inherent self-similarity of graphs, enabling more robust and efficient information transfer. This research combines established quantum information theory with graph theory to develop a new approach for quantum key distribution (QKD) and potentially quantum computation. The core claim is that this algorithm offers a pathway to achieve higher fidelity and increased resilience in quantum information encoding through the exploitation of graph structure. This work details the algorithm's design, the underlying mathematical foundations, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the potential for improved performance.

title: Quantum Error Correction via Topological Qubits in Photonic Networks
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is crucial for realizing practical quantum computation. However, the fragility of quantum states to environmental noise poses a significant challenge. This work proposes a novel approach to QEC utilizing topological qubits encoded within photonic networks. Topological qubits, characterized by their robust topological properties, offer inherent protection against local perturbations, making them ideal candidates for QEC. This architecture combines the advantages of both topological protection and the scalability offered by photonic networks. We present a theoretical framework for implementing a specific QEC code based on these principles, detailing the encoding process, error detection, and correction operations. The proposed system demonstrates enhanced resilience to noise compared to traditional qubit implementations. Key performance metrics, such as the surface code's logical error rate, are analyzed, highlighting the potential of this approach for achieving fault-tolerant quantum computation. The core of this method lies in the design of a photonic network tailored to efficiently implement the topological code, addressing limitations encountered in conventional qubit systems. Further investigation explores the impact of network topology and photon loss on the overall performance, proposing strategies for mitigating these effects. This research contributes to the ongoing effort to overcome the challenges of QEC and paves the way for building practical, scalable quantum computers.

title: Information Entropy Geometric Optimization
abstract: This paper explores a novel geometric optimization algorithm based on information entropy, aiming to enhance data distribution and compression efficiency. The core mechanism centers around constructing an "entropy mapping" graph, where information entropy serves as a fundamental geometric property. The algorithm iteratively adjusts data distribution to maximize entropy, while maintaining data integrity through a dynamic optimization process. Traditional approaches often focus on encoding, this work introduces a fundamentally different approach that leverages the non-linearity inherent in entropy to achieve superior compression and data management. The proposed method offers a promising pathway for more effective data compression and distribution strategies.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Bayesian Networks and Neural Turing Machines
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neuro-symbolic reasoning by integrating Bayesian Networks (BNs) and Neural Turing Machines (NTMs). The core challenge in neuro-symbolic reasoning lies in effectively combining the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks with the explicit logical inference of symbolic systems. Our proposed system leverages BNs to represent and reason with logical relationships, while NTMs are employed to learn and manipulate symbolic representations, thereby facilitating a hybrid system. We detail the architecture, training methodology, and demonstrate the potential of this integration for complex reasoning tasks. The key innovation is the dynamic interaction between these two components, allowing for both data-driven learning and rule-based inference. This approach addresses limitations of purely neural or purely symbolic systems, offering a pathway toward more robust and explainable AI. The system is designed to handle uncertainty and incorporate prior knowledge effectively. The ultimate goal is to create a reasoning engine capable of tackling intricate problems requiring both statistical inference and logical deduction.

title: 基于自适应神经网络的几何空间建模
abstract: This paper introduces a novel geometric space modeling framework based on adaptive neural networks. Traditional methods often rely on static, predefined models, limiting their ability to effectively handle complex geometric shapes. Our proposed framework leverages a dynamic adjustment mechanism within the neural network to achieve more precise and efficient geometric representation, offering a fundamentally new modeling paradigm. The core contribution lies in the implementation of a self-tuning neural network architecture that adapts its parameters and connections based on the input data, resulting in improved accuracy and robustness. The framework demonstrates significant improvements in modeling complex geometric structures, particularly when dealing with intricate shapes and variations.

title: 基于量子纠缠的非线性约束优化
abstract: This paper presents a novel non-linear constraint optimization algorithm based on quantum entanglement. Traditional constraint optimization methods often struggle with complex, high-dimensional constraints, leading to suboptimal solutions. This work leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to introduce a fundamentally different approach to constraint exploration, offering the potential for enhanced optimization capabilities. We introduce a novel entanglement-based constraint formulation and a corresponding optimization framework, demonstrating its effectiveness through a series of challenging, real-world problems. The core mechanism centers around manipulating entangled states to effectively explore the solution space and guide the search toward optimal configurations. This paper explores the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize constraint optimization, offering a promising path toward more efficient and robust solutions.

title: Quantum Bayesian Inference for Uncertainty Quantification in Machine Learning
abstract: Quantum Bayesian Inference (QBI) offers a promising approach to quantifying uncertainty in machine learning models, particularly in the face of adversarial examples. This paper introduces a novel framework for QBI that leverages quantum mechanics to enhance model robustness. We demonstrate improvements in uncertainty quantification through a rigorous analysis of the impact of quantum noise on model predictions. The core mechanism involves utilizing quantum state tomography to construct a quantum representation of the model's uncertainty, which is then used to generate robust predictions. We also explore the potential of QBI to mitigate adversarial examples through a novel defense mechanism based on quantum entanglement. This work presents a significant advancement in uncertainty quantification techniques, addressing limitations of existing methods and opening new avenues for reliable machine learning.

title: Time Scale Generalization in Neural Networks
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to neural network design, termed "Time Scale Generalization," addressing the inherent limitation of existing models that typically assume a fixed time scale. The core idea is to incorporate time scale-dependent non-linear activation functions, enabling networks to effectively process and generalize across varying temporal dynamics. We achieve this by leveraging the Gamma distribution and embedding time scale as a parameter within the activation function's non-linearity. This allows the model to adapt to signals with diverse time scales, improving its robustness and predictive capabilities. The presented framework offers a significant step toward more flexible and adaptable neural networks, particularly relevant for applications dealing with complex, time-varying data. The model is formulated mathematically, providing a clear and concise representation of the underlying principles.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Forced Outage Risk Prediction: Benefits and Comparison to Machine Learning
abstract: This study examines the ability of large language models (LLMs) to predict the risk of weather-related forced outages in the distribution grid in a zero-shot framework, without labeled training data. The problem is formulated as a binary severity classification task across three forecast horizons (3h, 6h, 12h), using six years of outage records and high-resolution weather data for a utility service area in central Texas. Four zero-shot LLMs are benchmarked against two supervised classifiers across two input configurations: one using current weather observations and the other using weather forecast data. Results show that supervised models outperform LLMs on macro-F1 and precision, while newer LLM generations achieve competitive scores. Beyond accuracy, LLMs offer complementary strengths in actionable reasoning and geographic scalability, suggesting that combining them with supervised models may be the best practice.

title: Circuit-Level Loss Performance of RHG and Foliated Floquet Color Codes in a Compound Photon--Atom Quantum Architecture
abstract: A central question for fault-tolerant quantum computing is which quantum error-correcting codes are best suited to a given hardware architecture. Here we compare the Raussendorf--Harrington--Goyal (RHG) code, the Foliated Floquet Color Code (FFCC), and the reduced FFCC in a compound photon--atom architecture that directly generates measurement-based quantum computation (MBQC) resources with near-deterministic photon--atom CZ gates. RHG serves as a natural benchmark, while the FFCC variants allow us to study whether reduced graph degree improves performance under an architecture-aware circuit-level loss model with delayed heralding and correlated bond-loss propagation. We construct two generation schemes compatible with the compound hardware and evaluate circuit-level thresholds under periodic boundary conditions. RHG achieves the highest circuit-level threshold, 2.75%, and its threshold falls below that of reduced FFCC only for large excess loss on intermodule CZ connections. RHG also achieves the lowest logical error rate in most resource-matched comparisons, but some low-loss windows favor reduced FFCC. Overall, we show that when the hardware supports the native gates and connectivity required for MBQC, the benefits of lower graph degree must be weighed against each code's intrinsic IID loss tolerance, generation-scheme details, and hardware-aware resource overhead.

title: A computational approach to maximum likelihood thresholds for colored Gaussian graphical models
abstract: Gaussian graphical models (GGMs) are essential tools for interpretable structure learning. However, in high-dimensional, small-sample regimes, the available data is often insufficient for the maximum likelihood estimator to exist. Colored Gaussian graphical models (CGGMs) mitigate this limitation by imposing symmetry constraints through graph coloring, which reduces the required sample size. This minimal number of observations needed to guarantee that the estimator exists almost surely is defined as the maximum likelihood threshold (MLT). Here, we address the computation of the MLT for CGGMs by focusing on its geometric formulation: finding the minimum rank of a sample covariance matrix such that its projection lies almost surely within the interior of the cone of sufficient statistics. We establish a unified theoretical framework, extending results from uncolored to colored models and introducing new symbolic algorithms. Furthermore, we present a computational study integrating sampling with topological data analysis (TDA) to investigate the local geometry of the cone of sufficient statistics. Our results demonstrate the potential of TDA to overcome the computational bottlenecks of traditional symbolic algebraic methods, particularly Groebner basis computations, in analyzing the likelihood geometry of CGGMs.

title: WeaveMark: Robust and Scalable Multi-bit LLM Watermarking via Coded Payload Spreading
abstract: Multi-bit watermarking for large language models enables content source tracing by embedding user-identifiable messages into generated text. Existing methods face a fundamental trade-off among extraction accuracy, text quality, and payload capacity. We propose WeaveMark, a robust and scalable multi-bit LLM watermarking scheme based on coded payload spreading. WeaveMark shifts this trade-off frontier by improving payload capacity through multi-bit-per-token spreading (weaving), improving extraction accuracy through soft-decision error-correcting codes, and preserving text quality through unbiased multilayer reweighting. It further introduces dedicated zero-bit layers for reliable watermark presence detection. Extensive experiments demonstrate substantial gains in extraction performance, especially for long messages and edited text, without degrading text quality. WeaveMark achieves an 89.8% match rate for 32-bit messages at 200 tokens, compared with 20.8% for BiMark. Under 10% substitution attacks on 16-bit messages at 200 tokens, it maintains 86.0% versus 30.7%. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/WeaveMark-ED6F.

title: AEGIS: An Auditable Evidence-Governed Interface for Cost-Aware AI Harness Selection in Finance
abstract: In bank onboarding, an accurate model output may remain non-executable until required evidence and approvals are in place. Obtaining them consumes money, compute, and human capacity and adds latency, yet may unlock a higher-value action. We introduce the Auditable Evidence-Governed Interface for Selection (AEGIS), a cost-aware framework that selects among versioned, pre-commit-mediated harnesses by conditioning jointly on task information, policy, evidence, budget, deadline, and runtime health. At fixed resource and risk prices under a stationary cell law, our frontier theorem identifies the support gap \(D(\theta)\) as the per-decision value of governance information. This value vanishes exactly when each task fibre has a common cost-adjusted optimum; otherwise, task-only routing incurs \(T D(\theta)\) expected structural pseudo-regret. LP duality yields auditable supporting prices for resources and risk; independent read-once evidence packages admit an exact assurance-option rule. Five repeated outer-CV evaluations of 1,000 borrowers show that governance-conditioned routing lowers normalised loss .099 versus task-conditioned routing (borrower-by-repeat 95\% sensitivity interval [.081,.116]) and .090 versus a training-selected fixed policy [.066,.111]; operations loss falls 33.2\% for .018 higher business loss. Across 629 matched cells in four tool-use suites, AEGIS supplies nine of ten cell-weighted and 14 of 15 equal-suite observed nondominated safety--risk--latency--call points. At one resource price, descriptive held-out-goal estimates show 7.31 points higher safe completion, .79 points lower attack success, 1.788 fewer seconds, and .113 fewer calls than suite-fixed. Signed evidence certifies lineage and specified checks, not factual correctness.

title: 基于量子自适应的概率图搜索
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic graph search algorithm, dubbed "Quantum Adaptive Probability Search" (QAPS), that leverages quantum self-adaptation to enhance exploration within complex search spaces. Traditional probabilistic graph search methods often suffer from inefficiency, particularly in problems with intricate search landscapes. QAPS employs a quantum-inspired self-adaptation mechanism to dynamically restructure the graph, facilitating more efficient exploration and ultimately, the identification of optimal solutions. We demonstrate the algorithm's efficacy through a series of benchmark problems, highlighting its superior performance compared to established methods in terms of both search time and solution quality. The core mechanism centers around the creation of a quantum-informed probability graph, allowing for adaptive node and edge weights, which significantly improves the algorithm's ability to navigate challenging search spaces.

title: Quantum Topology Information Matrix
abstract: Quantum topology information matrix (QTIPM) represents a novel approach to quantum information processing and communication, leveraging the unique properties of quantum topology. This research investigates the construction and application of a QTIPM framework to model and analyze the intricate relationship between topological structures and quantum states, offering a pathway towards enhanced quantum information handling and secure communication. The core claim is that this framework provides a more precise and efficient method for describing and manipulating quantum information compared to traditional matrix-based approaches. This paper explores the theoretical foundations, algorithm development, and potential applications of QTIPM, highlighting its advantages in understanding and exploiting quantum topology.

title: Quantum State Graph Topology Analysis
abstract: Quantum State Graphs (QSGs) are a fundamental framework in quantum information theory, representing the entangled states of qubits. This paper introduces a novel approach to QSG topology analysis, leveraging graph theory to effectively characterize and manipulate the structure of QSGs. We propose a method that utilizes graph traversal and connectivity analysis to identify and quantify key topological features, allowing for the optimization of quantum algorithms. The core mechanism focuses on establishing a robust and efficient framework for studying the topology of QSGs, ultimately contributing to advancements in quantum computation and information processing. title: Title: Quantum Information Theory Based on Topological Data Analysis
abstract: Quantum Information Theory (QIT) represents a burgeoning field seeking to harness the unique properties of quantum mechanics for computation, communication, and sensing. A significant challenge lies in effectively managing and manipulating quantum information, particularly concerning entanglement – a fundamental resource for quantum technologies. This research explores a novel framework combining Topological Data Analysis (TDA) with quantum mechanics to address this challenge, focusing on the detection and manipulation of entanglement. We propose a new type of topological measure, designed to be highly sensitive to the quantum state of a system, and utilize TDA to generate data that reveals critical states and facilitates the propagation of quantum information. The core claim is that this approach offers a fundamentally new way to understand and control entanglement, potentially leading to advancements in quantum cryptography and information processing.

title: Societies of Narrow Minds: A Comparative Analysis Review of Multi-Agent Systems and Emergent Cooperation
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Multi-Agent Systems and Emergent Cooperation in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of multi-agent and cooperation as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Recursive Quantum Topological Transformation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel recursive quantum topological transformation algorithm designed to automatically generate complex topological structures within quantum states, and subsequently, to facilitate precise control and manipulation of these states. Traditional approaches to quantum topology computation rely on manual design, limiting the generation of intricate topological landscapes. Our algorithm employs a recursive process, iteratively constructing and refining topological features to achieve precise control and transformation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of theoretical analyses and initial experimental explorations, highlighting its potential to significantly advance the field of quantum information processing and quantum computation.

title: A Physics-Based Cognitive Architecture Model
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to cognitive architecture design by leveraging physics simulation. Instead of relying solely on psychological and neuroscientific models, we aim to represent human cognitive processes as physical systems, utilizing their movement and interactions to mimic cognitive functions. The core claim is that human cognition can be effectively abstracted through the dynamics of physical systems. The proposed model utilizes concepts from mechanics, thermodynamics, and information theory to formalize cognitive processes. Specifically, attention is modeled as a force gradient directing movement, memory as a state-dependent energy system, and decision-making as a stochastic process influenced by environmental forces. We explore the emergent properties of these simulated systems, seeking to understand the fundamental principles underlying human cognition. This approach offers a new perspective on cognitive architecture, providing a tangible and quantifiable framework for studying complex cognitive phenomena. The model's output provides insights into potential limitations of purely computational models and suggests avenues for hybrid approaches combining physical simulation with traditional cognitive modeling techniques.

title: Based on Simulated Annealing Algorithm for Solving Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents an improved approach to solving complex optimization problems using the simulated annealing (SA) algorithm. The core challenge in applying SA to real-world problems lies in its susceptibility to getting trapped in local optima, particularly within high-dimensional search spaces and under complex constraints. This work addresses this limitation by introducing novel modifications to the algorithm's probability distribution and fitness evaluation functions. The primary goal is to enhance the search strategy of SA, ultimately improving its efficiency in finding global optimal or near-optimal solutions. The proposed method demonstrates an enhanced ability to navigate complex landscapes, offering a more robust and effective solution for a wider range of optimization challenges. The improvements significantly impact the algorithm's performance, allowing it to tackle more intricate problems where traditional SA methods often struggle. The theoretical framework and conceptual design are outlined, focusing on the practical implementation and potential applications of this refined SA approach.

title: 基于动态拓扑嵌入的神经元网络学习
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to neural network learning based on dynamic topology embedding. The core idea is to leverage the physical connections between neurons within a neural network architecture, dynamically adjusting them through a reinforcement learning framework. This contrasts with traditional methods that primarily focus on weight optimization. We propose a mechanism where a reinforcement learning agent learns to modify the network's topology—specifically, the weights associated with connections between neurons—to enhance information flow and improve learning efficiency. The theoretical framework is presented, outlining the key components of the system, including the neural network architecture, the reinforcement learning agent, and the topology embedding process. We demonstrate, through a mathematical model, how this dynamic approach can potentially overcome limitations associated with static network structures, leading to more adaptive and efficient learning. The work highlights the potential of topology-aware learning as a new paradigm in neural network design.

title: Topological Information-Driven Quantum Computation Topology Evolution
abstract: This paper explores the application of topological information to quantum computation, focusing on the evolution of quantum states through topological structures. The core claim is to design an algorithm that simulates the topological evolution of quantum states, allowing for predictive analysis of future quantum computations. Traditional quantum computation relies on classical physics models, but this research leverages quantum computation's inherent properties to offer a novel approach to simulating complex quantum systems. The algorithm employs a system of nodes and edges representing topological configurations, allowing for the observation of evolving topological structures. The paper details the design of a simulation framework, explores the impact of various topological parameters, and presents preliminary results demonstrating the algorithm's ability to predict state evolution. This work contributes to the development of robust quantum computing algorithms by focusing on the dynamic interplay of topological structures.

title: Temporal Graph Neural Networks with Contextual Drift Modeling
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have achieved remarkable success in various domains, including social network analysis, recommendation systems, and knowledge graph reasoning. However, a significant limitation of traditional GNNs is their inability to effectively handle evolving graph structures and temporal dependencies. This paper proposes a novel Temporal Graph Neural Network (TGNN) architecture, incorporating a Contextual Drift Model, designed to address this challenge. The TGNN learns and predicts the rate of change in node and edge attributes over time, explicitly modeling the concept of "contextual drift." This information is then integrated into the GNN's message-passing process, allowing the model to adapt dynamically to changing graph dynamics. The core mechanism utilizes a recurrent neural network (RNN) layer to capture the temporal evolution of attributes. The resulting TGNN demonstrates improved performance in scenarios where graph structures and node/edge attributes change over time, offering a more robust and adaptable solution compared to static GNNs. The primary contribution lies in the integration of temporal dynamics and contextual information within a graph neural network framework, paving the way for more sophisticated and reliable graph representations in dynamic environments.

title: Automated Program Code Generation via Multi-objective Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the novel approach of utilizing multi-objective optimization (MOO) techniques to automate the generation of program code. The core concept revolves around formulating program design challenges as multi-variable optimization problems, leveraging the capabilities of MOO algorithms to identify code variations that maximize desired program characteristics (e.g., performance, resource utilization, energy efficiency). This approach bypasses traditional, often manual or rule-based, code generation methods. The research investigates the potential of MOO to discover code solutions that are not explicitly conceived by human programmers, potentially leading to improved program efficiency and novel design paradigms. The paper details the framework for this process, including the selection of appropriate MOO algorithms, the definition of objective functions, and the subsequent code generation based on the optimization results. The core claim is that MOO can effectively automate code generation, while the core mechanism is the translation of program design problems into a multi-variable optimization framework for efficient code discovery.

title: Title: Fractal Geometry-Based Quantum Entanglement Preservation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, is notoriously fragile, susceptible to decoherence – a loss of quantum coherence due to interaction with the environment. Traditional methods for preserving entanglement often struggle with the inherent complexity of quantum systems and the unavoidable effects of measurement. This paper explores the application of fractal geometry – specifically, the concept of entanglement 'fractality' – as a novel approach to safeguarding quantum states. We propose a new method for generating highly correlated quantum states, utilizing a mathematical framework to quantify entanglement 'fractality' and guiding quantum circuit design to minimize decoherence. This investigation aims to advance our understanding of entanglement preservation and potentially unlock new avenues for quantum information processing.

title: KGXL-Query: Extending SPARQL with Semantic Search and LLM Functionality for Question Answering over Heterogeneous Data
abstract: The quest to answer complex questions, those requiring both structured facts and contextual evidence from unstructured data, has shown a gap in knowledge systems: the incompatibility between symbolic and semantic inference. Knowledge Graphs (KGs) support formal, logically grounded querying via structured languages such as SPARQL. Conversely, LLMs (Large Language Models) and semantic text search offer broad knowledge coverage through vector-based similarity metrics. However, beyond using KGs for refining text or LLM results, and complementing missing information in KGs via LLMs or text search, there is less emphasis on accessing LLMs & semantic text search functionality through SPARQL. Moreover, existing Question Answering (QA) methods on heterogeneous data sources use RAG, data unification, and decompose-and-aggregate methods. The unifying approaches suffer from irreversible information loss; decomposition-driven methods are prone to cascading errors; and RAG methods lack explainability and are limited to shallow textual integration. Therefore, we introduce KGXL-Query, a new SPARQL functionality extension that embeds LLMs and semantic search directly into SPARQL, enabling hybrid inference where symbolic and non-symbolic methods coexist within a single, executable, and explainable framework. Additionally, KGXL-Query paves the way by transforming the question to leverage the model rather than altering the data to fit it. Our experiments on four heterogeneous QA datasets show that KGXL consistently outperforms existing methods across all four benchmarks.

title: Finding a Shortest Vector and More in $2^{n/2+o(n)}$ Time using $q$-ary Coset Difference Tree
abstract: This paper presents a new randomized algorithm for solving the exact shortest vector problem. For the $n$-dimensional lattice $\mathcal L$, our algorithm runs in time and space $2^{n/2+o(n)}$. Our algorithm can be viewed as a $q$-ary analogue of the midpoint Hessian for an odd prime $q$; more precisely, we use the fact that, for a shortest vector $v$, the gradient (rather than Hessian) of the periodic Gaussian function at $v/q$ is nearly proportional to $v$ (up to sign), even after aggregation over a relatively large random affine coset. We compute the relevant coset gradient along a chain of intermediate lattices using a combinatorial procedure inspired by Wagner's generalized birthday algorithm, yielding the $2^{n/2+o(n)}$ time and space complexity. A variant of the algorithm solves the exact closest vector problem on every input $(y,\mathcal L)$ with a distance guarantee $\operatorname{dist}(y,\mathcal L)\le 1.039λ_1(\mathcal L)$ within the same time and space complexity. This guarantee holds for a random target and a random lattice drawn according to the Haar-Siegel measure. Thus, this algorithm solves a closest vector problem on such random instances in time and space $2^{n/2+o(n)}$.

title: Beyond static responses: multi-agent LLM systems as a new paradigm for social science research
abstract: Abstract As large language models (LLMs) transition from static tools to fully agentic systems, their potential for transforming social science research is well recognized. This paper introduces a structured framework for understanding the diverse applications of agentic LLM systems, ranging from simple data processors to complex, multi-agent systems capable of simulating emergent social dynamics. By mapping this developmental continuum across six levels, the paper clarifies the technical and methodological boundaries between different agentic architectures, surveying current capabilities and future potential. It highlights how lower-tier systems streamline conventional tasks like text classification and data annotation, while higher-tier systems enable new forms of inquiry, including the study of group dynamics, norm formation, and large-scale social processes. However, these advancements also raise challenges around reproducibility, ethical oversight, and emergent biases. The paper critically examines these concerns, arguing for sound validation methods, interdisciplinary collaboration, and standardized evaluation metrics. It argues that while agentic LLM systems offer considerable potential for the social sciences, using them responsibly will require careful, context-sensitive deployment and ongoing methodological refinement. The paper concludes with a call for future research that balances technical innovation with ethical responsibility, working toward agentic systems that not only replicate but also extend social science methodology.

title: MSE-CDO: A Multi-Strategy Enhanced Cloud Drift Optimizer for Global and Constrained Engineering Optimization
abstract: Cloud Drift Optimization (CDO) is a recent nature-inspired metaheuristic with a simple adaptive search framework. Despite its adaptive mechanisms, CDO does not explicitly regulate initial space coverage, population dispersion during evolution, or agent-specific local refinement. This study proposes a Multi-Strategy Enhanced Cloud Drift Optimizer, termed MSE-CDO. First, randomized multistart maximin Latin hypercube sampling is employed to improve the spatial distribution of the initial population. Second, adaptive Gaussian mutation is introduced after the original CDO update to generate controlled perturbations according to the population dispersion and search stage, while greedy selection retains better candidates. Third, a directional pattern search mechanism is incorporated to strengthen local refinement through individual search directions and adaptive step lengths. The proposed algorithm is evaluated on unimodal and multimodal benchmark functions and constrained engineering design problems and is compared with the original CDO and several established metaheuristic algorithms. The experimental results show that MSE-CDO improves the performance of the original CDO on most benchmark functions, achieves the best overall Friedman rank among the compared algorithms, and obtains competitive solutions for the considered engineering problems. These results indicate that the proposed strategies improve the search and convergence performance of CDO while preserving its original framework.
