title: 基于量子自适应的图论算法优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum self-adaptative graph theory algorithm designed for optimization. Traditional graph theory algorithms often struggle with large, complex graph structures, limiting their applicability. This work proposes a new algorithm leveraging quantum self-adaptative principles to dramatically improve the efficiency of graph operations, particularly in scenarios involving intricate connectivity patterns. The core mechanism centers around quantum state manipulation and entanglement to facilitate faster and more precise graph traversal and analysis. This approach promises to offer a significant advancement in graph optimization techniques, potentially impacting a broad range of fields including network analysis, data mining, and machine learning.

title: Variables from Actions: Canonical and Robust Reconstruction of Causal Coordinates from Intervention Composition
abstract: This preprint develops a recognition theorem for determining when a finite monoid of experimentally distinguishable, sequentially composable effects is exactly the monoid of partial hard interventions on a finite variable signature. Intrinsic minimal idempotents act as candidate value setters. Under atomic generation and a commutation-or-mutual-overwrite law, atom noncommutation determines candidate variable classes; a cardinality criterion is necessary and sufficient to exclude hidden collisions and yield a canonical representation. The paper proves uniqueness up to renaming, classifies the automorphism group, supplies explicit obstruction certificates and a quadratic-time checker for a supplied Cayley table, and gives a finite-sample recovery guarantee under separated Bernoulli response profiles. The scope is operational: the result does not recover a causal graph, statistical independence, or an ontology beyond the available intervention repertoire. A targeted literature audit through 2 September 2026 supports only a scoped novelty claim; absolute priority is not asserted.

title: Contextual Graph Embeddings with Hierarchical Temporal Memory
abstract: Graph embeddings have become a cornerstone of modern graph analysis, enabling the representation of graph structures in continuous vector spaces. However, traditional graph embedding methods often struggle to effectively capture complex dependencies, particularly long-range dependencies and hierarchical relationships inherent in many real-world graphs. This work proposes a novel approach—Contextual Graph Embeddings with Hierarchical Temporal Memory (CGH). We leverage the principles of Hierarchical Temporal Memory (HTM), a biologically inspired neural network architecture designed for learning and representing hierarchical temporal patterns, to enhance graph embeddings. The core idea is to integrate graph embedding techniques with HTM, allowing the model to learn contextual representations that simultaneously capture spatial and temporal relationships within the graph. This results in embeddings that are more robust and informative compared to those generated by conventional methods. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the CGH approach through theoretical analysis and a detailed explanation of the methodology, highlighting its potential for applications in areas such as social network analysis, knowledge graph reasoning, and anomaly detection. The key contribution lies in the fusion of graph embedding's representational power with HTM's ability to model complex, multi-scale patterns.

title: Adaptive Kernel Learning for Unsupervised Feature Extraction
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to unsupervised feature extraction using adaptive kernel learning. The core challenge in traditional kernel methods lies in the manual specification of kernel functions, a process that significantly restricts their applicability across diverse datasets. To address this limitation, we propose a method that automatically learns the kernel function itself using a recurrent neural network (RNN). This adaptive kernel approach allows the model to discover optimal kernel structures directly from the data, based on the underlying data distribution. The learned kernel can then be used for dimensionality reduction, clustering, or classification tasks. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and outline potential applications. The primary contribution is a method for automated kernel selection, opening up the potential of kernel methods to a much broader range of problems and potentially revealing previously unknown feature relationships.

title: Adaptive Algorithm Optimization Based on Biological Neural Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel adaptive algorithm optimization approach inspired by biological neural networks. The core idea is to mimic the self-organizing and adaptive learning mechanisms found in biological systems to automatically tune the parameters of optimization algorithms. We construct an adaptive learning mechanism based on a biologically inspired neural network, incorporating synaptic plasticity and dynamic neural network connections to achieve automated parameter adjustment. This approach aims to enhance the efficiency and performance of optimization algorithms by leveraging the inherent adaptability of biological systems. The research focuses on the theoretical design and conceptual framework, without involving experimental validation.

title: Secure Multi-Party Computation via Bio-Inspired Cellular Automata
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to secure multi-party computation (SMPC) leveraging the principles of cellular automata, inspired by biological systems. The core idea is to model participants in a computation as cells within a cellular automaton (CA) network, where information exchange occurs through local interactions. This architecture enables secure secret sharing and computation without revealing individual inputs to other participants. We present a framework for designing SMPC protocols based on CA rules, detailing the mechanisms for key generation, secret distribution, and computation itself. The resulting system offers a potentially robust and scalable solution for secure computation, drawing parallels to the inherent resilience and decentralized communication found in biological cells. The key contributions lie in the novel application of CA models to security and the development of a framework for formalizing the design of secure SMPC protocols using this approach. We explore the potential advantages, including improved resilience against malicious participants and a natural approach to fault tolerance, compared to traditional SMPC methods. The design emphasizes local interaction, reducing the communication overhead and enhancing privacy. ---

title: Based on Quantum Entanglement Optimization of Long-Distance Communication Protocols
abstract: This paper investigates the limitations of quantum entanglement-based long-distance communication protocols primarily due to coherence losses. A novel approach is presented that optimizes entanglement protocols to enhance communication distance and information transmission rates. The core of this method involves designing new entanglement generation and distribution schemes aimed at minimizing coherence degradation and maximizing communication efficiency. Specifically, we introduce a dynamic entanglement allocation strategy coupled with adaptive entanglement purification techniques. The proposed framework addresses the inherent challenges of maintaining entanglement fidelity over extended distances, ultimately aiming to surpass the current distance constraints associated with quantum entanglement communication. The theoretical analysis demonstrates improved performance metrics, including increased communication range and enhanced information transfer rates, relative to existing protocols. This work contributes to a more practical realization of long-distance quantum communication by mitigating coherence losses and offering a pathway towards scalable entanglement-based networks.

title: Dynamic Neural Network Topology Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural network optimization by dynamically learning and adapting its neural network topology using reinforcement learning. The core idea is to allow the network to autonomously adjust its neural connections through iterative topology optimization, thereby improving efficiency and robustness in handling evolving input data distributions. We introduce a "topology energy" function to quantify the irregularity of the neural network topology. A reinforcement learning agent interacts with a simulated environment (input data) to reduce this topology energy while simultaneously optimizing network performance metrics such as accuracy or latency. The topology updates are guided by a combination of local gradient information and global performance evaluations. This approach represents a departure from traditional weight-tuning methods, mirroring biological neural systems and offering the potential for adaptive and robust neural network architectures. ---

title: 基于自适应的图神经网络的拓扑学习
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to graph neural network (GNN) learning, leveraging an adaptive graph neural network (AGNN) to dynamically learn the graph topology and subsequently utilize this topology for data modeling. Traditional GNNs typically rely on static graph structures, limiting their ability to effectively capture complex relationships within the data. This work introduces an AGNN that adapts its network architecture and weights to the specific graph structure, enhancing the model's capacity to represent and extract meaningful information. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through several experiments, showcasing improved data modeling and analysis efficiency compared to existing approaches.

title: Computational Complexity of Graph Isomorphism with Quantum Algorithms
abstract: Graph isomorphism, the problem of determining whether two graphs are structurally identical despite potentially differing node labels and edge orientations, is a fundamental problem in computer science and theoretical mathematics. This paper investigates the potential for quantum algorithms, specifically leveraging Grover's algorithm, to improve the efficiency of graph isomorphism testing. We explore the theoretical complexity of this problem on a quantum computer, analyzing the impact of graph structure and algorithm parameters. The core claim is that determining graph isomorphism remains a computationally challenging problem, even with quantum acceleration. We delve into the limitations imposed by the problem's inherent complexity and the practical hurdles involved in implementing quantum algorithms for this task. The analysis focuses on the search space reduction offered by Grover's algorithm and its interaction with the graph's topology. We examine the factors that contribute to the algorithm's effectiveness, including graph size, connectivity, and the number of possible graph configurations. Ultimately, this work contributes to a deeper understanding of the computational challenges associated with graph isomorphism and provides insights into the potential and limitations of quantum computing in tackling this problem.

title: 基于自适应几何变换的神经网络架构
abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture, termed "Adaptive Geometry Neural Network" (AGNN), designed to enhance model generalization by dynamically adjusting network parameters in response to input data geometry transformations. Traditional neural networks struggle with this adaptability, often requiring extensive hyperparameter tuning. The AGNN leverages a self-adaptive geometric transformation mechanism to automatically adjust network parameters, offering a significant improvement in robustness and performance across various datasets and scenarios. We present a detailed explanation of the architecture, its key components, and results demonstrating the benefits of this approach.

title: Relational Reinforcement Learning with Abstract State Spaces
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has achieved remarkable success in various domains, but its performance often degrades when faced with high-dimensional state spaces. Traditional RL algorithms struggle to efficiently explore and learn in environments where the raw sensory input is complex and lacks inherent structure. This paper proposes a novel approach, Relational Reinforcement Learning with Abstract State Spaces (RRLASS), that addresses this limitation by introducing a learned abstraction layer. This layer transforms raw sensory input into a compact, relational state space, enabling RL agents to operate effectively in complex, high-level environments where direct representation of raw data is impractical. We formulate the core mechanism around the idea of relational representation learning, where relationships between elements within the state are emphasized, allowing the agent to generalize better and learn faster. The key innovation lies in the integration of this relational representation with standard RL algorithms, resulting in a system that can handle abstract state spaces with improved efficiency and performance. We explore the theoretical foundations of this approach and present a preliminary analysis of its potential.

title: Rewards, Regrets, and Rubber Arms: A Comparative Analysis Review of Reinforcement Learning in Games and Robotics
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Reinforcement Learning in Games and Robotics in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of reinforcement learning and robotics as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Should We Make the Bots More Human?
abstract: This chapter provides a conceptual synthesis of anthropomorphism in customer-facing conversational agents. It examines how humanlike chatbot cues shape customer perceptions, behaviours, and relationship outcomes in conversational marketing. Drawing on anthropomorphism theory, the Computers Are Social Actors perspective, social presence theory, relationship marketing, and service-dominant logic, the chapter develops a framework linking design cues to psychological mechanisms and customer responses. It argues that chatbot humanness is not a universal design advantage but a context-dependent resource. Humanlike cues can support trust, engagement, disclosure, satisfaction, intentions, and relationship quality when they fit the task, journey stage, capability, privacy context, and transparency. The same cues can intensify creepiness, privacy concern, anger, blame, resistance, and disappointment when they inflate expectations or obscure machine agency. The chapter concludes with guidance and future research directions for calibrating chatbot humanness across marketing and service contexts.

title: Quantum-Assisted Memory-Efficient Training for Parameter-Intensive Wi-Fi-Based Human Activity Recognition
abstract: Wi-Fi-based human activity recognition (HAR) has become an important part of integrated sensing and communications, paving the way for a range of context-aware services. However, most existing Wi-Fi-based HAR systems rely on deep learning (DL) models that are computationally and memory intensive in both training and inference, which poses significant challenges for real-world deployment. Conventional training requires simultaneous updates of millions of parameters, leading to prohibitive memory consumption. In this paper, we propose a novel quantum-assisted memory-efficient training framework (Q-MET) designed to improve efficiency in both training and inference. Q-MET utilizes a hybrid quantum classical neural network to indirectly generate parameters for HAR models, significantly reducing the trainable parameter count compared to direct optimization. To further support the deployment on resource-constrained devices, we integrate structured pruning during the training phase. Experimental results demonstrate that Q-MET achieves a 90% to 95% reduction in trainable parameters compared with conventional backpropagation-based DL training while maintaining or even exceeding classical classification accuracy. Additionally, Q-MET supports lightweight inference through structured pruning, achieving 75% to 85% model sparsity with less than 2% loss in classification accuracy. To the best of our knowledge, this work represents the first quantum-assisted approach to simultaneously tackle memory inefficiencies in both the training and inference stages of HAR systems.

title: Progressive Pseudo-Label Optimization for Point-Supervised Change Detection
abstract: Point-supervised change detection (PS-CD) aims to identify pixel-level changes between bi-temporal images using only sparsely annotated points. Although point annotations substantially reduce labeling costs, their limited spatial coverage often results in incomplete and noisy pseudo-labels. To address this issue, we propose a two-stage framework that introduces SAM2 priors into PS-CD and progressively adapts them to the target task. In Stage I, SAM2 generates object-aware candidate masks from point annotations on the bi-temporal images, and a bi-temporal mask selection strategy is designed to convert generic segmentation responses into more reliable change pseudo-labels. Subsequently, a lightweight CNN refinement module with an uncertainty-aware loss is employed to improve boundary quality and local structural consistency. In Stage II, we construct a teacher-student self-training framework in which the teacher is updated by exponential moving average and periodically refreshes the pseudo-labels. This design establishes a closed-loop optimization process that alternates between pseudo-label refinement and model re-optimization. Experiments on three benchmark datasets, including WHU-CD, LEVIR-CD, and SYSU-CD, demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms previous weakly supervised approaches on most benchmarks and remains competitive with several fully supervised methods.

title: Accurate Virtual Re-staining of Frozen Section Microscopy Images Using a Two-Stage Deep Learning Framework
abstract: Frozen section analysis (FSA) provides rapid histopathological information during surgery, supporting timely surgical decision-making. However, the rapid freezing process is prone to introducing ice crystal artifacts in the acquired optical microscopy images, which compromise tissue structural integrity and degrade image quality, increasing the diagnostic difficulty for pathologists. To address this issue, this paper proposes a two-stage deep learning model named AI-FSA to realize accurate optical virtual re‑staining and quality assessment of intraoperative frozen section microscopy images. AI-FSA couples an improved CycleGAN-based unsupervised stain transfer with a Vision Transformer (ViT)-based quality assessment module to computationally remove ice crystal artifacts and provide feedback on diagnostic confidence. We constructed an unpaired frozen‑paraffin section dataset covering five tissue types and two section thicknesses, and validated the approach using objective optical image quality metrics and blinded evaluation by three pathologists. The results show that the optically virtual-stained images achieve significantly improved sharpness and color fidelity while preserving key tissue structures. Blinded evaluation further confirms that the virtual-stained images exhibit high similarity to real paraffin sections across multiple perceptual metrics. AI-FSA provides significant clinical potential for improving the efficiency and reliability of intraoperative frozen section diagnosis by enhancing the optical presentation of tissue morphology.

title: Replication Package of "Integrating Human Knowledge Through Action Masking in Reinforcement Learning for Operations Research"
abstract: This repository contains the code and problem instances of our paper "Integrating Human Knowledge Through Action Masking in Reinforcement Learning for Operations Research".The code and instances of each problem are provided in a separate folder. The code of the stochastic problems uses random seeds to deterministically reproduce the results provided in the paper.paint_shop_problem/ contains the code and instances of the deterministic paint shop problem. Please unzip the zip-file paint_shop_data.zip to a folder "Data/"load_management_problem/ contains the code the stochastic load management problem.inventory_problem contains the code of the stochastic inventory management problem.Each folder contains a Run.bat file, which starts several processes to distribute the effort for policy learning. Trained reinforcement learning policies and logfiles of mean reward over time will be stored in the folders "Models/" and "Logs/". These folders are created automatically by the scripts. The main scripts are "Run_Experiments.py", which also accept several command line parameters. The Run_Experiments.py scripts (when called by Run.bat) generate multiple output csv-files, which you then have to merge before aggregating the final results.In addition, each folder contains a script AnalyzeResults.py, which reproduces all aggregated results and the statistical test results. In the paint shop problem, aggregated results are directly provided as csv files.The package was tested under Python 3.14.6 and the following packages:gymnasium 1.3.0stable-baselines3 2.9.0torch 2.13.0numpy 2.5.0pandas 3.0.3The hyperparameters are generally set to the default values of stable-baselines3 (except timesteps, entropy coefficient, and target KL divergence). Please see the supplementary materials for the full list of PPO hyperparameters.

title: Where Perceptrons Meet Proof Trees: A Interdisciplinary Mapping Review of Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning Systems
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning Systems in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of neuro-symbolic and reasoning as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: 基于动态模块的语言的逻辑验证
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to logical verification utilizing a dynamically modular language. Traditional logical verification methods rely on manually designed rules, limiting flexibility and scalability. Our system automatically generates and modifies logical rules during program execution, enabling more sophisticated reasoning and validation capabilities. We introduce a dynamic modular language designed to facilitate this automation. This work explores the design and implementation of this system, demonstrating its potential to significantly enhance the capabilities of logical verification through dynamic rule generation. The core mechanism centers around a rule engine that adapts to the program's execution, automatically updating and refining the logical framework. This results in a more robust and adaptable verification process. We will present a prototype demonstrating the system's functionality and discuss its limitations and future directions.

title: Title: Temporal Pattern Embedding via Quantum State Collapse
abstract: Quantum state collapse offers a novel approach to encoding and manipulating temporal patterns, representing complex sequences with enhanced computational efficiency. This paper explores the application of quantum state collapse to create a method for embedding temporal patterns into a quantum state, enabling efficient reconstruction and analysis of these patterns. We propose a quantum algorithm that leverages the inherent properties of quantum states to capture the temporal evolution of the embedded pattern, offering a potential advancement over existing methods. The core mechanism centers around the controlled collapse of a quantum state towards a pre-defined pattern, facilitating a streamlined reconstruction process. This work addresses limitations in current pattern embedding techniques, particularly concerning computational complexity and the ability to efficiently analyze complex sequences. We present a rigorous theoretical analysis and initial experimental validation demonstrating the feasibility and potential of this approach.

title: Quantum Neural Networks: A Novel Non-linear Activation Function Design
abstract: Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) hold immense promise for revolutionizing artificial intelligence, offering the potential to tackle complex problems currently intractable for classical neural networks. A crucial component of QNNs is the network architecture and the activation functions that govern the flow of information. This paper explores the design of a novel non-linear activation function specifically tailored for QNNs, focusing on its ability to promote self-organizing connectivity and enhanced information transfer. We introduce a concept of "self-regulation" within the activation function's design, aiming to enhance the network's expressiveness and robustness. This research employs a rigorous mathematical analysis and demonstrates its potential to significantly improve the performance of QNNs across various tasks. The core mechanism involves manipulating the activation function's output to encourage specific patterns in the network's connectivity.

title: Dynamic Matrix Quantum State Generation
abstract: This paper explores a novel method for generating dynamic quantum states using a matrix-based approach. The core principle revolves around leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement to create a versatile set of quantum states through controlled manipulation. We propose a system that dynamically constructs quantum states by orchestrating the evolution of a matrix, allowing for a flexible and potentially powerful representation of quantum information. This approach contrasts with conventional methods that rely on predefined states, offering the opportunity for enhanced information storage and transmission capabilities. The proposed method is presented as a foundation for advanced quantum data handling, potentially enabling novel applications in quantum computing and information science.

title: Quantum Non-Linear Geometry Field Theory: Adaptive Displacement
abstract: Quantum non-linear geometry field theory offers a novel framework for addressing computationally challenging problems in quantum information processing, particularly in quantum error correction and quantum communication. This paper proposes a quantum displacement algorithm based on entangled states, leveraging the self-adaptative properties of entanglement to achieve faster, more robust, and potentially self-correcting displacement. We explore the potential of this approach to overcome limitations in current quantum computation, specifically focusing on the challenges presented by classical information transfer. The core mechanism centers on the design of a quantum displacement algorithm that utilizes entangled states for adaptive adjustment, introducing a potential pathway for quantum error correction. We discuss the theoretical foundations, potential challenges, and preliminary results of this approach, highlighting its novelty and implications for the future development of quantum information processing.

title: Learning Continuous Representations from Streaming Data with Echo State Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Echo State Networks (ESNs) for learning continuous representations directly from streaming data. Traditional recurrent neural networks (RNNs) often struggle with the challenges posed by continuous data streams, particularly the need for extensive training datasets. ESNs, with their inherent reservoir structure and adaptive learning rules, provide a compelling alternative. This work details a framework for utilizing ESNs to efficiently learn and adapt to evolving data distributions within a continuous stream. The core contribution lies in the design of an Echo State Network reservoir optimized for capturing the temporal dynamics of streaming data, enabling robust and scalable representation learning. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical analysis and outline key design considerations for practical implementation. The primary goal is to provide a computationally efficient and data-sparse solution for continuous representation learning, addressing a critical limitation of conventional RNNs.

title: Information Entropy Enhanced Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces an Information Entropy Enhanced Algorithm (EIA) for enhancing the generalization ability of machine learning models, particularly in the presence of sparse datasets. Traditional machine learning methods often rely on gradient descent, which struggles with data sparsity. The EIA employs a novel gradient update mechanism based on information entropy to proactively optimize model parameters, mitigating overfitting and improving generalization performance. The core mechanism involves introducing a tailored weighting scheme that dynamically adjusts the influence of each parameter based on the entropy of the data distribution. The paper details the algorithm's implementation, provides a comparative analysis of its performance against established methods, and concludes with a discussion of its potential applications and future research directions.

title: 基于动态拓扑结构的自适应优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on dynamic topology structures. Traditional optimization methods often rely on manual design and can be hampered by inherent limitations. This algorithm leverages the inherent topological properties of the problem domain to automatically adjust the structure, thereby reducing computational complexity. The core mechanism centers around the manipulation of topology to guide the search process, leading to improved efficiency and effectiveness. We present a framework for implementing this algorithm and demonstrate its efficacy on several benchmark problems, highlighting its advantages over existing approaches.

title: Information-Theoretic Latent Variable Models for Anomaly Detection
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to anomaly detection utilizing information-theoretic principles within a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) framework. Traditional anomaly detection methods often rely heavily on reconstruction error, which can be misleading when dealing with complex, high-dimensional data. Our method, termed Information-Theoretic Latent Variable Modeling (ITLVM), directly incorporates information-theoretic metrics such as mutual information and entropy into the latent variable space of the VAE. This allows us to identify anomalies as deviations from the expected information flow patterns inherent in the data. Specifically, the VAE is trained with information-theoretic regularizers, encouraging the latent space to represent meaningful information structures. Anomalies are detected by monitoring the reconstruction error alongside information divergence from the expected distribution, leveraging a threshold-based approach. We demonstrate the effectiveness of ITLVM through conceptual analysis and formulation, highlighting its potential advantages over conventional anomaly detection techniques. The core claim is that directly employing information-theoretic metrics within the latent variable modeling framework provides a more robust and fundamental approach to anomaly detection.

title: Adaptive Probability Programming Language
abstract: This paper introduces a novel programming language, the Adaptive Probability Programming Language (APPL), designed to address the limitations of traditional, static programming paradigms in uncertain and dynamic environments. APPL fundamentally shifts the paradigm by allowing programs to dynamically adjust their probability distributions during execution, based on observed program behavior and external conditions. This core mechanism, driven by continuous monitoring and adaptation, aims to enhance program robustness, adaptability, and ultimately, decision-making accuracy in scenarios characterized by inherent uncertainty. The language incorporates a unique syntax and runtime system to facilitate this dynamic adaptation, offering a fundamentally new approach to programming. We outline the key features, design considerations, and potential applications of APPL, highlighting its ability to move beyond static assumptions and embrace the reality of probabilistic systems. ---

title: Codes over Frobenius Ring T
abstract: This paper focuses on the construction and analysis of codes over the Frobenius ring T. By exploiting the idempotent structure of the ring, codes over T are decomposed into direct sums of component codes over a related local Frobenius non-chain ring. A gray map is constructed and shown to be bijective and distance-preserving, allowing code parameters to be determined from their gray images. Linear codes and cyclic codes over the considered ring are completely characterized, and explicit descriptions of their generating sets and cardinalities are obtained. The duals of cyclic codes are also examined, and the gray map is shown to preserve orthogonality and self-duality. Well-parameterized codes were obtained over the ring T.

title: WireSeg-32K: A Physics-Grounded Synthetic Dataset for Wire Instance Segmentation
abstract: Deformable linear objects such as wires and cables are difficult to segment because they are thin, highly deformable, and frequently self-occluded, while large-scale instance-level annotations are expensive to obtain in real scenes. Existing resources either focus on cable tracing or semantic segmentation under constrained settings, or generate visually plausible images without physically grounded wire deformation. We present WireSeg-32k, a synthetic dataset for wire instance segmentation with 32,000 RGB images, instance masks, depth maps, and a complementary real-world test set with annotations. To generate this dataset, we develop DeformX, a co-simulation pipeline that couples Cosserat-rod dynamics with photorealistic Isaac Sim rendering, enabling physically plausible, contact-consistent wire shapes, CAD-based wire assets, and diverse visually grounded scenes. As a simple baseline, LoRA fine-tuning SAM3 on WireSeg-32k alone improves real-world mAP@75 by 10.2% over the off-the-shelf model, showing that physically grounded synthetic data can transfer to real wire perception.

evidence.abstract: Deformable linear objects such as wires and cables are difficult to segment because they are thin, highly deformable, and frequently self-occluded, while large-scale instance-level annotations are expensive to obtain in real scenes. Existing resources either focus on cable tracing or semantic segmentation under constrained settings, or generate visually plausible images without physically grounded wire deformation. We present WireSeg-32k, a synthetic dataset for wire instance segmentation with 32,000 RGB images, instance masks, depth maps, and a complementary real-world test set with annotations. To generate this dataset, we develop DeformX, a co-simulation pipeline that couples Cosserat-rod dynamics with photorealistic Isaac Sim rendering, enabling physically plausible, contact-consistent wire shapes, CAD-based wire assets, and diverse visually grounded scenes. As a simple baseline, LoRA fine-tuning SAM3 on WireSeg-32k alone improves real-world mAP@75 by 10.2% over the off-the-shelf model, showing that physically grounded synthetic data can transfer to real wire perception.

title: Variational preparation of thermofield double states for SYK models via multi-angle QAOA: sequential angle pruning for circuit reduction
abstract: Variational preparation of thermofield double (TFD) states can require deep quantum circuits, particularly for interacting many-body systems. Reducing these circuits while retaining high fidelity is therefore crucial for TFD-state preparation on noisy quantum processors. We study this problem by applying the multi-angle quantum approximate optimization algorithm (ma-QAOA) to TFD-state preparation and introducing two top-down sequential angle-pruning algorithms. Starting from the optimized initial ma-QAOA circuit, both algorithms sequentially remove Pauli-string evolutions with small optimized angles and reoptimize the remaining parameters after each removal. We apply these algorithms to Gaussian and binary Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev (SYK) models in both dense and sparse cases. We find that ma-QAOA prepares the target TFD states with high fidelity and that sequential small-angle pruning retains high fidelity while reducing the circuit depth, particularly at low temperature. Moreover, using the post-reoptimization cost in sequential small-angle pruning further improves the fidelity. For the binary sparse $N=10$ SYK model at $β=10$, $88.8\%$--$92.1\%$ of the nonlocal Pauli-string evolutions are removed while retaining an average fidelity of approximately $95\%$. Finally, we propose extensions of the sequential pruning algorithms toward quantum--classical hybrid implementation.

title: Eliciting ESG Preferences for Reinforcement Learning-Based Portfolio Optimization
abstract: Modern portfolio management increasingly demands a balance between traditional risk-adjusted returns and strict Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) mandates. Current Reinforcement Learning (RL) approaches typically optimize for a single ESG provider, neglecting the significant divergence in rating methodologies across the industry and the unintuitive nature of manually weighting conflicting objectives. This paper addresses these limitations by formulating ESG-aware portfolio optimization as a Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning (MORL) problem that simultaneously incorporates ratings from three distinct ESG agencies. To bridge the gap between high-dimensional algorithmic trade-offs and human decision-making, we integrate a Preference Elicitation framework using Gaussian Processes. This system enables practitioners to infer their latent utility functions through intuitive pairwise comparisons of candidate portfolios based on their Sharpe ratios and aggregate ESG scores. We systematically evaluate our framework by employing Large Language Model (LLM) personas to simulate Portfolio Managers operating under varied regional contexts. Empirical results using historical market data reveal that regional backgrounds fundamentally shift the derived preference weights. For instance, European-based personas tend to prioritize ESG alignment over financial returns, while Texas-based personas favor risk-adjusted performance. This work offers a highly adaptable framework that successfully aligns multi-objective algorithmic trading with diverse, real-world human sustainability preferences.

title: A Study to Analyze the Role of Artificial Intelligence in Enhancing Customer Experience in Digital Marketing
abstract: Customer experience has become a key differentiator for organisations operating in increasingly digital markets, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) is now widely used to make digital marketing faster, more personalised and more responsive. This study examines the role of AI in enhancing customer experience in digital marketing, with special reference to SSR Compressor Service, an industrial air-compressor sales and service organisation based in Chennai. The study adopts a quantitative, descriptive and analytical cross-sectional research design. Primary data were collected from 31 respondents through a structured questionnaire covering four composite constructs — AI accessibility and use (QTotal), AI-enabled personalisation and interaction (ATotal), responsiveness and convenience (CTotal), and overall customer experience (ETotal) — and analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, multiple linear regression, and Cronbach’s alpha reliability testing. All four composite measures were positively and significantly correlated with one another (r = .615 to .892, p < .001). A multiple regression of the three predictor composites on overall customer experience was statistically significant, F(3,27) = 28.626, p < .001, explaining 76.1 percent of the variance (R² = .761, Adjusted R² = .734). CTotal (Beta = .640, p < .001) and ATotal (Beta = .565, p = .022) emerged as significant unique predictors of customer experience, while QTotal did not retain a significant unique effect once the overlapping variance among the predictors was accounted for. Reliability testing confirmed good internal consistency across all scales (alpha = .730 to .869). The findings suggest that AI can meaningfully enhance digital customer experience when it is implemented as a supporting technology built around personalisation, convenience and responsiveness rather than as a replacement for human interaction, and the study offers practical recommendations for SSR Compressor Service and similar industrial businesses. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence; Digital Marketing; Customer Experience; Personalization; Chatbots; Customer Engagement; Trust.

title: Certified Branch Reductions for the Binary Covering Number K_2(11,3)
abstract: Technical report, software, and authenticated proof records for the binary covering-code cell K_2(11,3). Exact structural certificates and a complete normalized partition close 112 of 150 normalized branches, leaving 38. Within four selected unresolved third-word children, checked RUP and DRAT certificates close 324 of 350 exhaustive fourth-word branches, leaving 26 and closing no complete child or normalized parent. The exact value remains open and the known interval 15 <= K_2(11,3) <= 16 is unchanged.

title: Qubits of a Feather, Flawed Together: A State of the Art Review of Quantum Computing Architectures Compared
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Quantum Computing Architectures Compared in the context of Physics. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of quantum computing and qubits as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Physics.

title: Quantum Entanglement Self-Organizing Computation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum entanglement for self-organizing computation, proposing a novel framework leveraging the unique properties of entangled states to achieve substantial scaling and resource optimization. Traditional parallel computing relies on classical algorithms, while our work introduces a quantum entanglement-driven approach offering enhanced computational capabilities. The core mechanism centers around constructing a "quantum entanglement self-adaptive" system, designed to automatically adjust resource allocation and maximize efficiency. We demonstrate the framework's capabilities through simulations, illustrating its potential to significantly outperform classical approaches in certain scenarios. The research lays the groundwork for a paradigm shift in computational design, moving beyond traditional parallel processing towards a fundamentally different approach.

title: Title: Non-Linear Predictive Coding with Adaptive Bias
abstract: The field of predictive coding offers a powerful framework for modeling sequential data by emphasizing the role of prediction and adaptation. Traditional methods often employ fixed biases that can hinder the model's ability to accurately represent complex data dynamics. This paper introduces a novel approach to non-linear predictive coding, termed "Dynamic Bias Engine," which dynamically adjusts the bias towards specific patterns based on observed data. We demonstrate that this mechanism significantly enhances the model's capacity to detect subtle shifts in data, offering a substantial improvement over current approaches. The core concept is to create a feedback loop that continually refines the bias, improving predictive accuracy. This work expands the concept of predictive coding by introducing a mechanism that adapts the bias towards specific patterns based on the observed data, rather than a fixed, predefined bias.

title: Adaptive Evolutionary Algorithm-Based Hardware Architecture Design
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to hardware architecture design utilizing the Adaptive Evolutionary Algorithm (AEA). The core idea is to leverage the power of evolutionary computation to automatically generate and optimize hardware architectures, aiming to achieve superior performance and reduced power consumption. The methodology involves defining a search space encompassing various architectural parameters, employing the AEA to explore this space, and evaluating the resulting architectures based on predefined performance metrics. The key innovation lies in the adaptive nature of the AEA, which dynamically adjusts its search strategy based on the fitness of the explored solutions, leading to more efficient and targeted architecture exploration. This approach offers a significant improvement in hardware design efficiency and performance compared to traditional, manually-designed methods. The paper outlines the design process, the AEA implementation, and demonstrates the potential of this technique for diverse hardware applications.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Geometric Intuition
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum mechanics to revolutionize geometric intuition, proposing a novel framework centered on quantum superposition and entanglement to provide a more precise and intuitive understanding of shapes and their relationships. The core claim is that by leveraging these quantum phenomena, we can move beyond classical geometric models to a deeper, more nuanced representation of geometric concepts. This work investigates the implications of this approach, focusing on the potential for enhanced visualization, the development of new mathematical tools, and a broadened perspective on geometric analysis. The paper outlines the fundamental concepts, proposes a preliminary model, and discusses future research directions.

abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for adaptive geometry transformation based on quantum entanglement. This work leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust geometric transformations, resulting in significantly improved efficiency and potential for more sophisticated geometric modeling. We propose a framework that utilizes entangled states to represent and manipulate geometric parameters, enabling a form of self-optimization during the transformation process. The core mechanism involves creating entangled mappings between geometric transformations and the underlying parameter space. This allows for a continuous and nuanced optimization of the transformation process, surpassing the limitations of traditional approaches. The paper details the algorithm's design, provides a preliminary implementation, and analyzes its potential benefits and challenges in the context of geometric transformations.

title: Quantum State Compression via Topological Quantum Spines
abstract: Quantum state compression is a crucial challenge in quantum information science, aiming to significantly reduce the volume of quantum states required for storage and transmission. Traditional approaches often rely on complex algorithms and significant computational resources. This paper proposes a novel quantum state compression technique based on topological quantum spines, leveraging the unique properties of topology to efficiently compress quantum states. We detail the core mechanism of the method, including the utilization of quantum entanglement and topological transformations to identify and eliminate redundant information within the quantum state. Our analysis demonstrates that this approach offers improved efficiency and potential applications compared to existing quantum compression methods. The study explores the theoretical foundations of the proposed technique and presents preliminary experimental results to validate its effectiveness.

title: Based on Quantum State Superposition Distributed Storage System
abstract: This paper proposes a novel distributed storage system leveraging the principles of quantum state superposition. The core idea is to encode data into superposition states and store them across a network of distributed quantum computers. This approach aims to significantly enhance storage capacity and efficiency compared to classical methods. The system utilizes the inherent parallelism offered by superposition, allowing for the simultaneous storage and retrieval of multiple data sets. The theoretical framework is presented, outlining the key components and operational principles of the system. We explore the fundamental mathematical concepts underlying this system, focusing on quantum state representation, superposition, and entanglement. The design emphasizes scalability and resilience, addressing potential challenges associated with distributed quantum computing environments. This research contributes to the emerging field of quantum information storage, paving the way for high-density data storage solutions. ---

title: Quantum-Driven Constraint Optimization for Molecular Dynamics Simulations
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum computing to revolutionize molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, addressing the significant computational bottleneck currently limiting their widespread adoption. We propose a novel quantum algorithm, specifically leveraging quantum annealing, to efficiently navigate the complex conformational landscape of molecules, leading to dramatically accelerated simulations. The core claim is that this algorithm offers a significant improvement in speed and accuracy compared to traditional MD methods, particularly for large molecule systems. We detail the design of the quantum algorithm, its potential advantages, and preliminary results demonstrating its efficacy in a simplified model.

title: Dynamic Topological Dependency Learning (TDDL)
abstract: This paper introduces Dynamic Topological Dependency Learning (TDDL), a novel approach to knowledge representation and reasoning that addresses the limitations of static knowledge graphs in dynamic environments. The core claim is that a knowledge representation with a dynamically adaptable topology, informed by real-time environmental perception and continuous interaction feedback, can achieve greater efficiency and reliability in reasoning compared to traditional static knowledge graphs. TDDL utilizes multi-modal sensor data – including visual, auditory, and tactile information – to perceive the environment in real-time and combines this with feedback from the agent's actions (success/failure, speed, direction, etc.). Leveraging reinforcement learning, the system dynamically adjusts the topological structure of the knowledge graph by strengthening high-correlation connections and weakening low-correlation ones. This dynamic adjustment reflects both knowledge updates and environmental adaptation. Furthermore, a "Dependency Prediction Module" proactively forecasts potential dependencies and constructs related connections. The key innovation lies in the system's ability to automatically construct and adapt its knowledge representation based on real-time sensory input and interaction, fostering a deeper integration between knowledge and the environment, and ultimately enhancing generalization and robustness in complex, dynamic scenarios.

title: Analyzing Meaning in Situated Multimodal Interactions
abstract: This thesis is about how meaning can be represented, identified, and interpreted in situated multimodal interactions. There have been impressive advances in dialogue systems in recent years, culminating in the development of large language models capable of responding to prompts with fluent, natural-looking text. However, when humans communicate with each other, they use multiple modalities beyond language; for example, gesture. Understanding the meaning conveyed through gesture and other communicative modalities is crucial for artificial intelligence systems to effectively interact with humans in embodied settings. Moreover, such systems must also be able to perform situated grounding, linking communicated information to the outside world.

title: Distilling deep optical flow stereo methods to retrieve dense three-dimensional wind fields
abstract: Geostationary atmospheric motion vectors (AMVs) provide the dense horizontal wind vectors (u,v) and heights ingested into data assimilation systems. Traditional AMVs track features using window-based cross-correlation and estimate heights via infrared brightness temperatures paired with numerical weather prediction (NWP) background states, creating a circular dependency that yields inaccurate heights, high computational cost, and sparse retrievals. Stereo winds from GEO-GEO and GEO-LEO geometrically resolve heights from parallax shifts across different poses, eliminating NWP dependence and improving accuracy, but they remain computationally heavy with limited coverage. In this work, we replace window-based tracking in stereo matching with deep optical flow for efficient, improved retrieval. Fine-tuning balances a self-supervised geometric residual loss with supervised radiosonde reconstruction. To eliminate multi-satellite overlap requirements, we distill the stereo teacher into a single-satellite student model. Chi-square and height uncertainties from the teacher are emulated by the student for quality assurance. The student generates winds across full-disk GEO imagery globally. Validation compares stereo and student models against radiosondes, operational AMVs, ERA5 reanalysis, and EarthCARE cloud profiles. Results through triple collocation show that stereo winds improve performance beyond operational AMVs for water vapor bands (6.2, 6.9, and 7.3 μm), wit degradation in the long-wave infrared (11.2 μm) band.

title: DANSur_HM: Modularly incorporating higher modes in a deep learning based gravitational-wave surrogate
abstract: Numerical relativity (NR) simulations provide the most faithful representation of the gravitational waves (GWs) emitted by binary black hole (BBH) systems during merger. In the context of GW astronomy, tasks such as parameter estimation can require vast numbers of waveform evaluations per second across the entire parameter space. Since performing full NR simulations for each evaluation is not computationally feasible, interpolating methods for existing NR waveforms, known as surrogate models, have been developed with marked success. In this paper, we build on our previous work to introduce methods to train a fast surrogate model based on neural networks in order to generate BBH merger waveforms, including the fundamental (2,2) mode, as well as the (3,3), (2,1), (4,4), (3,2), (4,3) and (5,5) higher-order modes. Applying a pretraining step on approximant data before fine-tuning on NR data allows us to smooth out the parameter space, and making use of the parallelization ability of GPUs to project the NR waveforms in the inclination-phase (ι, ϕ) sphere during training allows the fitting of all the explored modes simultaneously. The developed surrogate model, DANSur\_HM, achieves average mismatches of the order of 10^{-4}, with the worst mismatch at 2.5times10^{-3}, and achieves throughput above 6times10^5 waveforms/second on an NVIDIA V100 GPU. Parameter estimation tests confirm the usefulness of the inclusion of higher modes.

title: LoFi RADIO: A Distilled In-Domain Backbone Applied for Artifact-Severity Grading of Ultra-Low-Field Neonatal Brain MR
abstract: Ultra-low-field MRI makes neonatal brain imaging deploy- able in low-resource settings, but its low SNR, lack of shielding, and long scan duration make it especially prone to acquisition artifacts, motivating automated quality control. We address the LISA 2026 Task 1a challenge: multi-label severity grading (0/1/2) of seven common image artifacts on ULF T2 weighted volumes. We identify that a number of backbones may be successfully paired with a classification MLP, but that no single backbone is uniformly best across artifacts. To improve performance, we evaluate routing complementary foundation model teachers through a per-artifact gate, as well as distilling the teachers into a single in-domain ViT-S student (LoFi RADIO) over an unlabeled low-field MRI corpus. Both of these strategies improve the weighted composite. The distilled backbone matches or exceeds the gate and has the added advantage of not requiring deployment of multiple large foundation models at infer- ence.

title: DMRL: Document-Mediated Reinforcement Learning for Skill Optimization in Advertising Recommendation
abstract: Advertising recommendation requires continuously tuning complex system parameters while balancing commercial returns and user experience. Recent work has introduced large language models (LLMs) with skill documents to assist this labor-intensive process, but skill optimization remains largely prompt-driven, lacking a principled mechanism to attribute rewards to specific document edits. To address this limitation, we propose Document-Mediated Reinforcement Learning (DMRL), a skill self-evolution framework that models skill document optimization as a sequence of structured editing actions. In DMRL, an upper-level agent performs controlled document edits, while a frozen lower-level task agent evaluates their effects through A/B testing. To address credit assignment and long-term outcomes, we introduce two key components: (1) Dual-Relative Policy Optimization (DRPO), a post-training policy optimization method for robust and risk-aware advantage estimation; and (2) Long-term Reward Predictor (LRP), which estimates long-term outcomes by modeling population heterogeneity with disentangled representation learning and cross-attention transfer. DMRL was deployed on a large-scale short-video ads platform and extensive empirical evaluation shows that DMRL outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across key advertising metrics

title: Performance Comparison of Full and Hybrid QGANs for Particle Shower Simulation
abstract: The use of quantum generative adversarial networks (qGANs) is based on an efficient approach that simulates high-energy particle showers using a reduced model complexity. In this study, we analyze complete and hybrid qGAN architectures for the creation of particle shower images and compare their training behavior, convergence and accuracy. The results show a stable training of the entire qGAN, which can generate the general parameters of the shower well. The hybrid design also exhibits competitive performance with the medium discriminator yielding the highest accuracy of all the tested configurations. However, with a lower or higher discriminator the decrease of performance is due to the imbalance between the capacity of the generator and discriminator. The results show that quantum models can be represented with a much smaller number of trainable parameters, and still capture the representational capabilities of classical models, something that can be studied in greater detail with larger models and more sophisticated physics-based metrics.

title: The four contracts of PEVG
abstract: Four roles in a cycle. The planner receives the task and emits a plan of ordered steps with explicit dependencies; it has no authority outside the workflow and performs no tool actions. The executor receives a step and its capability contract and emits the result together with the action as actually performed; it is the only role with authority outside the workflow, that authority is an enumerated set of permitted operations, and it must not decide whether its own result is correct. The verifier receives a result and the acceptance criteria and emits accept, reject with a class, or abstain; it holds the epistemic boundary on what may be believed, has no authority outside the workflow, and must not produce the response. The generator receives the verified results and their decisions and emits the response with the claims it rests on; it must not assert anything the verifier did not pass, and where the verifier abstained it must omit the claim or mark it unsupported. Rejection returns to the role that can act on it. Each role writes its own evidence, and the four records together are the workflow's Execution Evidence; a single record written at the end by the generator does not satisfy this. This figure is Figure 1 of PEVG: Planner, Executor, Verifier, Generator, version 1.0, deposited at Zenodo. title: KEFE RG: Relational Grammar - State-Bearing Continuation, Conditional Trivalence, and Directed Event Composition
abstract: Abstract KEFE RG provides the structural admission layer of the KEFE technical publication suite. It develops a history-bearing relational grammar that separates candidate generation, admissibility testing, same-sector evolution, and structure-changing events. Within a declared pairwise graph branch, the paper derives mature trivalent counting and the unique smallest expanding endpoint . A directed event , carrying three matched past–future relations and a common closure, supports ordered composition while distinguishing admission from state transfer. The resulting framework specifies exact structural constraints and falsifiers without presupposing a metric, action, probability law, spectrum, or physical trajectory.

title: Quantum Topology Adaptive Optimization
abstract: Quantum Topology Adaptive Optimization explores the potential of quantum topology principles to revolutionize optimization techniques. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static parameter settings, limiting the system's ability to adapt and improve. This research investigates a novel quantum optimization algorithm that dynamically adjusts system parameters based on quantum topology, resulting in enhanced performance and robustness. The core mechanism leverages the inherent properties of quantum topology to create a self-optimizing framework. This paper presents a detailed theoretical analysis and experimental validation of this approach, demonstrating its potential to surpass conventional optimization methods in complex, dynamic systems.

title: 基于自适应的非线性优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive non-linear optimization algorithm designed to mitigate the effects of noise and uncertainty in input data. Traditional optimization methods often lack this capability, leading to unstable and suboptimal solutions. This algorithm dynamically adjusts optimization parameters based on the input data's characteristics, resulting in improved stability and robustness. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations and analysis, showcasing its superior performance compared to established methods in scenarios involving noisy data. The core mechanism leverages the inherent self-adaptation properties of the algorithm, enabling it to effectively handle complex data distributions.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Neural Network Graph Structure Modeling (DANDGM)
abstract: This paper introduces DANDGM, a novel framework for graph structure modeling based on dynamic adaptive neural networks. Traditional graph structure modeling methods often rely on static representations, limiting the model's flexibility. DANDGM leverages the inherent dynamism of neural networks to dynamically adjust graph parameters, enabling optimization of model performance. We present a comprehensive overview of the DANDGM architecture, detailing its core mechanisms and demonstrating its effectiveness through illustrative examples. This work offers a significant advancement in graph modeling, specifically focusing on enhanced model adaptability and improved performance compared to conventional approaches.

title: 拓扑几何的自适应算法设计
abstract: This paper explores the application of topology-based algorithms to automated algorithm design. Traditional algorithm design often relies on manual creation, while this approach aims to dynamically generate and optimize complex algorithms. The core mechanism involves leveraging the inherent topological properties of algorithms to guide the design process, leading to improved efficiency and performance. The study focuses on a novel algorithm design methodology that automatically generates and refines complex algorithms applicable to a diverse range of optimization problems. This research proposes a framework for utilizing topological concepts to streamline algorithm development, offering a potential paradigm shift in the field.

title: High-Dimensional Non-Linear Matrix Learning Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive learning algorithm for matrix representation and prediction. Traditional matrix learning methods often rely on handcrafted features, limiting their adaptability to complex datasets. This algorithm leverages data inherent information to dynamically adjust model parameters, mitigating overfitting and improving generalization performance. The core mechanism involves the implementation of a self-adaptive learning process that iteratively optimizes model parameters based on the data itself. This approach offers a significant advancement in machine learning, enabling more effective feature extraction and model representation, particularly when dealing with high-dimensional data. The research explores the potential of this algorithm to improve the performance of various machine learning tasks.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Counterfactual Reasoning in Causal Bayesian Networks
abstract: Counterfactual reasoning – the process of asking "what if" questions about interventions and their consequences – is a fundamental aspect of causal inference and decision-making. Current approaches to modeling and reasoning about counterfactual scenarios within causal Bayesian networks often rely on complex and potentially error-prone manual derivations or approximations. This paper proposes a novel approach utilizing probabilistic programming to directly address this challenge. We introduce a language that seamlessly integrates counterfactual inference into causal Bayesian networks, allowing users to define "what if" scenarios and automatically obtain the expected outcomes. The core of our system rests on the ability to represent causal relationships as probabilistic models and then leverage probabilistic programming techniques for efficient computation. This approach offers a more intuitive, robust, and scalable solution for counterfactual reasoning compared to existing methods, ultimately facilitating more informed decision-making based on causal understanding. The key contributions are a formalized language and a computational framework that automate counterfactual calculations within a causal Bayesian network setting.

title: E8‑Phased Quantum Synchronization Lattice (E8‑PQSL) — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: By mapping the 240 E8 root vectors onto a φ‑scaled lattice and driving each node at the 132 Hz base frequency, the resulting phase‑locked network can be used to synchronize entangled qubits across a distributed quantum processor. The φ coupling introduces a golden‑ratio phase offset between adjacent nodes, creating a self‑correcting interference pattern that suppresses decoherence. This lattice acts as a topological error‑correcting code, enabling fault‑tolerant quantum gates without the need for active feedback. The principle extends the E8‑RQFG by turning the static lattice into a dynamic, entanglement‑preserving scaffold for scalable quantum computation. Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: Title: Fractal Dimension-Aware Neural Network Architectures
abstract: Fractal dimension, a measure of complexity and self-similarity, is a pervasive phenomenon in nature and data science. Successfully representing this dimension within neural network activations is a significant challenge, hindering models' ability to capture intricate patterns. This paper explores the application of a novel "fractal-aware weighting scheme" to neural network architectures, aiming to improve the representation of fractal dimension in neuron activations. We introduce a new network design that dynamically adjusts connection strengths based on the observed fractal dimension of the activation maps, thereby enhancing feature extraction and improving the model's capacity to model complex, self-similar data. The core mechanism revolves around a refined weighting algorithm that prioritizes activations with fractal-like characteristics, leading to a more robust and nuanced representation of data. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through simulations and preliminary experiments on a dataset exhibiting fractal-like structures.

title: Dynamic Construction and Control of Quantum Entanglement Topological Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to constructing and controlling quantum entanglement networks leveraging programmable photonic crystals and topological defects. The core claim is the development of a dynamic network capable of adapting its topology and entanglement properties, moving beyond static, fixed architectures. This is achieved through the injection of topological defects within an array of photonic crystals, coupled with polarization control and time-resolved measurements. The system enables real-time manipulation of entanglement qubits and facilitates adaptive reconfiguration of the network topology. The key innovation lies in the dynamic control mechanism, addressing a significant limitation of existing topological quantum computing approaches which primarily rely on static network structures. The theoretical framework and underlying mechanisms are detailed, outlining a pathway towards scalable and adaptable quantum information processing. The presented methodology offers a fundamental shift in topology-protected quantum computation, paving the way for more flexible and robust quantum networks.

title: Distributed Federated Learning with Byzantine Fault Tolerance using Homomorphic Encryption
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models across decentralized devices while preserving data privacy. However, FL systems are vulnerable to Byzantine faults, where malicious participants introduce corrupted model updates, compromising the integrity of the global model. This paper proposes a novel framework for distributed federated learning with Byzantine fault tolerance, leveraging the power of homomorphic encryption. The system encrypts model updates using homomorphic encryption, allowing the central server to perform aggregation computations directly on the encrypted data. This approach eliminates the need for decryption, thereby safeguarding client data and providing robust protection against Byzantine attacks. The core claim of this work is that the combination of FL with homomorphic encryption provides a fundamentally secure and resilient solution for distributed model training. We detail the system architecture, the encryption and aggregation protocols, and analyze the security and performance implications. The proposed method significantly enhances the robustness of FL against malicious participants, offering a practical solution for privacy-sensitive applications.

The core claim of this work is that the combination of FL with homomorphic encryption provides a fundamentally secure and resilient solution for distributed model training. We detail the system architecture, the encryption and aggregation protocols, and analyze the security and performance implications. The proposed method significantly enhances the robustness of FL against malicious participants, offering a practical solution for privacy-sensitive applications.

title: Quantum State Sensing via Multivariate Correlation Measurements
abstract: This paper investigates the application of multivariate correlation measurements (MCM) to enhance the performance of quantum state sensors. Traditional quantum state sensing relies on single-variable measurements, often limited by the inherent uncertainties in the measured quantities. We propose a novel approach utilizing MCM to simultaneously extract information from multiple physical properties associated with a quantum state. This method leverages quantum entanglement and the correlations generated through MCM, allowing for a more precise determination of the state's parameters. The theoretical framework is presented, detailing the mathematical formulation of the measurement process and the potential for increased accuracy and information yield. We explore the underlying principles of entanglement and demonstrate how MCM can effectively mitigate the limitations of conventional single-variable sensing. The core claim of this work is that MCM provides a pathway for simultaneously extracting multiple physical properties from quantum state sensors, ultimately leading to superior measurement precision. Key aspects include the design of the measurement scheme, the mathematical analysis of the correlations, and the discussion of the implications for various quantum sensing applications.

title: Deep Learning for Modern E-Learning Systems
abstract: Models that learn from users and content interact at scale. This chapter articulates the many uses of highly layered neural networks in personalization, applied feedback, and text, speech, code, image, and video assistance. The main model families are described: CNNs, RNNs / LSTMs, transformers, autoencoders, and other generative models; as are the approaches to training, optimizing, regularizing, and deploying models. Representation learning from unstructured data, adaptive pathways, engagement and emotion detection, and predicting performance and studying are learning outcomes that guide model choice. System elements include data gathering, analytics, model serving in-cloud or on-device, and scale. Intelligent tutoring, recommendation, auto-grading, and dialogue systems on modern platforms are current use cases. Trade-offs include privacy, sparse supervision, bias, lack of explainability, seamlessness to legacy systems, and computation cost. Real-world deployments, both successful and not, are the focus of the illustrative case studies. The chapter's focus is on core techniques and design choices to build the next generation of e-learning systems.
